# CLI, MCP, and app channel reference

<!-- Generated by packages/mcp/src/reference.ts. Change that file or the definitions it reads, then run:
pnpm --filter @dohc/mcp exec vitest run src/reference.test.ts -u -->

Agents and developers use this page to work with dohc from outside the app. It lists every tool of the desktop MCP server, every `dohc` command, and every app channel request, with its arguments and what it returns.

## Connect

- **MCP.** In dohc, open **Settings**, then **Agents**. Select **Add agent**, choose **Another agent**, and copy the **MCP config** into your agent's MCP settings. Each agent's page also has its config. The server works on one workspace. The config ends with `--agent-id <id>`, so your agent posts under that agent's name and waits for its own messages. While a run is on, History shows changes in this workspace as that agent's. Use **Start run** and **Stop run** under **History** on the agent's page.
- **CLI.** The `dohc` command talks to the running dohc app, so keep dohc open. Run it inside the workspace folder. Agents that dohc starts have it on their `PATH`.
- **Share links.** A share link has its own MCP server, `dohc-share`, with other tools. This page does not list them. Its address is `/mcp/s/<secret>` on the share's server, where `<secret>` is the text after `#` in the link. Add that address to an MCP client that supports MCP sign-in. The client opens a consent page, and a person selects **Allow**. Anyone who has the address can do this and get the link's full access, so share it only as you share the link. The [share-web README](../../services/share-web/README.md) describes each step.
- **Personal agents.** An account's own agent has its own MCP server, `dohc-personal`, at `/mcp/agent/w/<workspaceId>` on the account's server. This page does not list its tools. Where the agent has Edit, `dohc_read_document` and `dohc_edit_document` read and edit a live document. They work only on a self-hosted server that runs its own session host. The owner must open the document in dohc on a desktop first. If a call answers with code `preparing`, call it again shortly. The [share-web README](../../services/share-web/README.md#live-documents) says what each other code means and what to tell the owner.

## Versions and changes

Agent prompts and scripts depend on these names. Before launch, a rename replaces the old name outright, with no alias.

- The desktop MCP server reports its version as `0.3.0`. A rename or removal of a tool, argument, or result field raises it.
- `--json` output carries `schemaVersion: 3`. A change to the shape of that output raises it.
- The CLI and the app must be the same build. Otherwise the CLI stops with `CLI/app version mismatch — restart the app`.

A tool or command that cannot do what was asked returns `{ ok: false, reason }`, or exits with status 1 and prints the reason. MCP marks such a result as an error.

A desktop MCP tool refuses an argument it does not take. The error names that argument and lists the ones the tool takes.

Partial form creation returns `{ kind: "partial", created, failedStage, reason, retry }`. The CLI exits with status 1 and keeps the structured output. MCP marks the result as an error and keeps its structured content.

## Desktop MCP tools

New to building in dohc with an agent? Start with [Build with agents](../how-to/build-with-agents.md) and the public agent skill at [`skills/dohc/SKILL.md`](../../skills/dohc/SKILL.md). The table below separates everyday building tools from internal sync and recovery tools.

When an agent connects, the server sends short instructions and serves the skill and its references as resources: `dohc://guides/skill`, `dohc://guides/collections`, `dohc://guides/apps`, `dohc://guides/automations`. `dohc://workspace/info` returns `{ workspaceId, name, rootPath, shareAccess }` for the served folder. Every tool carries the MCP hints `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, and `openWorldHint`. A tool that can both read and change data is marked as one that changes it.

**Core everyday building.** Start here for everyday apps, documents, Collections, SQLite imports, and workspace discovery.

### `dohc_list_workspaces`

List the local dohc workspaces in the desktop registry.

No arguments.

Returns `{ workspaces: { workspaceId, rootPath, kind, remote? }[] }`.

### `dohc_workspace_status`

Report whether this workspace is local-only or cloud-synced. In the owning workspace, also list live documents whose edits the server refused, as keptEdits, and shared notes whose edits wait for the server, as pendingShare, and new notes shared by a link or with a person, which the server has no file for yet, as pendingShareWhileOpen.

No arguments.

Returns `{ synced, scope, cloudConnected, credentialStatus, collectionsWaiting?, keptEdits?, pendingShare?, pendingShareWhileOpen?, heldFiles?, syncFailure?, workspaceId?, serverUrl?, syncPause? }`. `scope` is `"local"` or `"cloud"`. `collectionsWaiting` is `true` while Collection updates wait for a sync that has not finished. Files and documents still save. To continue offline, stop sync. `keptEdits` lists `{ path, reason, incident, recovery, saveOnly?: true }` for each live document whose edits the server refused. Pass them to dohc_save_recovery_copy, dohc_retry_kept_edits or dohc_stop_again. When saveOnly is true, save a recovery copy instead. If recovery is unreadable, retry reads the edits again. `pendingShare` lists the paths of shared notes whose edits wait on this computer for the server; each file holds older text until the server accepts them, and dohc_read_document returns the current text. `pendingShareWhileOpen` lists the paths of new notes shared by a link or with a person, which the server has no file for yet; each file is current here and reaches the server once its editor in dohc is left. A share made on another computer counts after dohc next lists the shares of this workspace. A shared view has none of `keptEdits`, `pendingShare` or `pendingShareWhileOpen`. In a shared view, `heldFiles` is `{ count, files, message }` while dohc holds shared files back. Each of `files` is `{ path, reason, owner? }`, where `reason` is `local-collision` (a file from this computer is in the way) or `spelling-collision` (this disk treats two shared names as one). `message` says what the person must do. After a `local-collision` file moves, refreshing the shared view in dohc brings the shared file in. Only the person who shared the files can fix a `spelling-collision`. `syncFailure` is `{ code, message, detail }` while sync is failing. A shared view has no `syncFailure`. `code` is stable, such as `server-unreachable` or `conflict-wait-limit`. `message` says what happened and what to do. `detail` is the raw error to report. These fields are absent when the dohc app cannot answer.

### `dohc_search_workspace`

Search across pages, Document Collections, typed records, transactional dataset pointers, and chats in one ranked call, with 1-hop linked context (wikilinks, Collection relations, chat mentions). Use this first to recall context in the owning workspace before listing files or grepping chat. Check complete, indexBuilding, policyDegraded, mountsCovered, sharedChannelRowsUncovered, and truncated for coverage.

Workspace search runs only on the owning workspace. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `query`: `string`. Required.
- `surfaces`: `("page" | "collection" | "record" | "chat")[]`
- `pathPrefix`: `string`
- `collectionPath`: `string`
- `includeNeighbors`: `boolean`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ versionId, results: { kind, id, title, path?, objectId?, collectionKind?, collectionPath?, datasetPath?, recordId?, fields?, recordCount?, matchedFields?, threadId?, messageId?, author?, createdAtMs?, channelName?, channelWireId?, linkedFilePath?, snippet, matchedTerms, related }[], neighbors: { kind, id, title, path?, objectId?, collectionPath?, recordId?, threadId?, snippet?, via }[], complete, indexBuilding, policyDegraded, mountsCovered, sharedChannelRowsUncovered, truncated }`.

### `dohc_read_document`

Read a Markdown document as it is now, including edits an open editor has not saved to the file yet. Read it before dohc_edit_document: edits match this text.

- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, markdown } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_create_document`

Create a Markdown document at a path that does not exist yet. `markdown` is its body text, without frontmatter. dohc writes it the way a person types into a new file, so later changes go through dohc_edit_document.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `markdown`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_edit_document`

Edit a Markdown document through dohc. A person editing it at the same time keeps their text and sees yours arrive. While someone may be typing in it, in an open editor or on a device it syncs to, an edit may change text inside blocks and add blocks, but not remove a block or change its kind. `find` is Markdown that occurs exactly once in the text dohc_read_document returns; it becomes `replacement`. Omit `find` to add `replacement` at the end. The edit changes the body, not the frontmatter. Pass `allowLossySourceSha256` (from dohc_read_file) only when confirming a rewrite of a lossy Markdown note that dohc cannot round-trip verbatim. It returns when the edit is saved. A pending `warning` means the edit is saved locally and the shared file update is pending; do not repeat the edit. Other warnings mean someone may be changing the same blocks; read the document to check. `requestId` is a random key you choose, such as a UUID. Sent again with the same key, after a timeout for example, the edit returns its first result instead of applying twice, while it runs and until 1,024 later keyed requests to this workspace have finished. dohc then refuses the key until 16,384 more have finished; after that, or after dohc restarts, the key can apply the edit again. Use a new key for each new edit, including one that redoes text a failed edit reported missing. If the call fails without a reason, read the document before you retry.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `allowLossySourceSha256`: `string`
- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `find`: `string`
- `replacement`: `string`. Required.
- `requestId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, changed, warning? } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_drawing`

Read an .excalidraw drawing as a compact element list: id, type, version, position, size, text, colors, links, groups, frames, text containers, and arrow bindings, plus its app state. An open canvas answers with what it holds now (live: true). Line, arrow, and freehand points are left out unless points is true; pointCount says how many there are. Pass each element's version as expectedVersion to dohc_edit_drawing. Owner workspace only.

Only the original workspace opens drawings live. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `points`: `boolean`

Returns `{ path, live, elements: { id, type, version, x, y, width, height, angle?, text?, strokeColor?, backgroundColor?, link?, groupIds?, frameId?, containerId?, startBinding?, endBinding?, boundElements?, points?, pointCount? }[], appState }`.

### `dohc_create_drawing`

Create a new .excalidraw drawing, optionally with elements, without replacing an existing file. History records it as yours. Each element is { type: rectangle|ellipse|diamond|text|arrow|line|frame, x, y } with optional id, width, height, text, strokeColor, backgroundColor, points, link, groupIds, and frameId. A text element with containerId sits inside that shape or arrow. An arrow takes start and end element ids to bind its ends. The answer lists each element's id and version. Undo Run in History skips a drawing an agent created, because removing a drawing can also remove linked assets: delete it individually from History. It also skips a drawing open in an editor until it closes. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `elements`: `({ x: number, y: number, width?: number, height?: number, text?: string, strokeColor?: string, backgroundColor?: string, points?: ((any JSON)[])[], link?: string | null, groupIds?: string[], frameId?: string | null, id?: string, type: "rectangle" | "ellipse" | "diamond" | "text" | "arrow" | "line" | "frame", containerId?: string, start?: string, end?: string })[]`
- `requestId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, elements: { id, version }[], warning? } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_edit_drawing`

Change an .excalidraw drawing: add elements, update fields of existing ones, or delete them. An open canvas shows the change at once and keeps what the person draws meanwhile. update and delete need each element's id and the version from dohc_read_drawing as expectedVersion; the whole edit is refused if someone changed one of those elements since, so read again and retry. Deleting a shape deletes its text too. Each element is { type: rectangle|ellipse|diamond|text|arrow|line|frame, x, y } with optional id, width, height, text, strokeColor, backgroundColor, points, link, groupIds, and frameId. A text element with containerId sits inside that shape or arrow. An arrow takes start and end element ids to bind its ends. Send requestId to retry safely: the same id answers again without applying twice. Undo Run in History skips a drawing an agent created, because removing a drawing can also remove linked assets: delete it individually from History. It also skips a drawing open in an editor until it closes. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `add`: `({ x: number, y: number, width?: number, height?: number, text?: string, strokeColor?: string, backgroundColor?: string, points?: ((any JSON)[])[], link?: string | null, groupIds?: string[], frameId?: string | null, id?: string, type: "rectangle" | "ellipse" | "diamond" | "text" | "arrow" | "line" | "frame", containerId?: string, start?: string, end?: string })[]`
- `update`: `({ x?: number, y?: number, width?: number, height?: number, text?: string, strokeColor?: string, backgroundColor?: string, points?: ((any JSON)[])[], link?: string | null, groupIds?: string[], frameId?: string | null, id: string, expectedVersion: integer })[]`
- `delete`: `({ id: string, expectedVersion: integer })[]`
- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `requestId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, elements: { id, version }[], warning? } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_query_collection`

Query a collection folder's indexed records: filter, sort, group, and page. Requires the workspace engine and the dohc app.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `filter`: `{ field: string, operator: "equals" | "contains", value: any JSON }`
- `sort`: `({ field: string, direction: "asc" | "desc" })[]`
- `groupBy`: `string`
- `resolveRelations`: `boolean`
- `limit`: `integer`
- `cursor`: `any JSON`

Returns `{ ok: true, collection: { path, status, reasons }, records: { id, path, conflicted, values }[], groups: { value, records }[] | null, nextCursor: { sortValues, recordPath, recordId } | null } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_record`

Read one collection record by id: current field values plus per-field history with author attribution. Requires the workspace engine and the dohc app.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `recordId`: `string`. Required.
- `historyLimit`: `integer`
- `beforeHistoryId`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, collection: { path, status, reasons }, record: { id, path, conflicted, values }, history: { historyId, field, previous, next, authorOriginId, actorKind, onBehalfOf, depth, recordedAtMs, linkAuthor, automationRun }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_create_record`

Create a Markdown record in a collection folder as the agent, optionally seeding fields, and return its record id. The kept map reports current values of seed fields preserved after someone edited them. On partial creation, retry with partial.retry.recordId and the same inputs to finish the existing record. Other taken names are refused.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `name`: `string`. Required.
- `recordId`: `string`
- `fields`: `{ [key: string]: any JSON }`

Returns `{ ok: true, recordId, recordPath, kept? } | { ok: false, reason, partial?: { kind: "partial", created, failedStage, reason, retry } }`.

### `dohc_set_record_fields`

Set fields on a collection record as the agent, e.g. fields: {"status": "done"}. The change lands in the record's live frontmatter, open desktop views update, and record history attributes it to the agent.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `recordPath`: `string`. Required.
- `fields`: `{ [key: string]: any JSON }`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, recordPath } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_dataset`

Create, prepare, approve, inspect, and use transactional Collections (dataset.json, SQLite tables, and approved operations) in the owning workspace. Address one with datasetPath, its dataset.json path relative to the MCP server folder, such as tracker/dataset.json, never a folder or datasetId; list returns these paths, and a move changes them. expectedDatasetId refuses the request when the path now names another Collection. create takes definition, a dataset.json descriptor object (formatVersion 1 or 2), and approves revision 1. prepare takes descriptorPath; approve takes its preparationId and revisionSha256. invoke runs an approved operation with its described revision and revisionSha256 and a stable idempotencyKey. Generated create operations take input { values: { <fieldId>: value } }, and edit operations add id and expectedVersion; field ids come from describe. Apps bind to these Collections and have no separate store. export writes a private recovery archive, with private records and retry credentials, to an absolute savePath outside the workspace. dohc://guides/collections lists every action's fields, migrations, history restore, permissions, and recovery.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `request`: the JSON object of one [`dohc dataset`](#dohc-dataset) verb, with the verb's name as `action`. Required.

Returns what that verb returns, listed under [`dohc dataset`](#dohc-dataset).

### `dohc_detect_apps`

Detect app folders in the workspace: web content a browser can open, found from index.html, package.json, dohc.json, and common web configs.

- `path`: `string`
- `maxDepth`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, apps: { root, title, kind, confidence, entry?, packageManager?, scripts, configuredPreviewMode?, buildOutputs, configPath?, diagnostics }[], count, detector }`.

### `dohc_create_app`

Scaffold an app folder with app.publish.json and src/App.tsx, which use React and dohc/ui from the built-in app kit. Requires dohc open. History records each file under your agent name. A partial failure lists the files already written.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `appRoot`: `string`. Required.
- `title`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, appRoot, files }`, or `{ ok: false, reason, written?, path?, currentSha256? }`. `written` lists files published before the first failure.

### `dohc_test_app`

Check an app folder without running it: detector diagnostics and entry presence. In a workspace you own, dohc_publish_app action verifyFrontend compiles and runs the app in dohc's sandbox.

- `appRoot`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok, app, checks: { name, ok, message?, path? }[] }`. `ok` is true when every check passes.

### `dohc_publish_app`

Verify, approve, launch, and publish a local app, a folder with app.publish.json, as its owner on this computer. verifyFrontend takes exactly one of appRoot or publicationId, then compiles and runs the app in dohc's offline sandbox against an empty ephemeral Collection without changing live data; run it before you approve or hand over an app. Local: prepareLocal, approve, then launchLocal. Share link: createLink with a stable operationId, so a retry returns the same link, then prepare and approve; these need a workspace that syncs with a server (see dohc_workspace_status). A link URL is a bearer credential: keep its secret yourself, never send it to dohc, and append the returned appQuery before the URL's fragment. In a workspace you joined, only Personal apps work. dohc://guides/apps lists every action, staging with Collection changes, apps for members, and Personal apps.

- `request`: `{ action: "verifyFrontend", workspaceId?: string, appRoot?: string, publicationId?: SHA-256 hex, versionId?: string, expectStartupBackend?: ({ op?: "backend.invoke" | "backend.attempt" | "backend.upload" | "backend.file" | "backend.external" | "collection.list" | "collection.create" | "host.copy" | "host.print" | "host.notice" | "unknown", operation?: string, status?: integer, refusalCode?: string })[], steps?: ({ kind: "waitFor", selector: string, textIncludes?: string } | { kind: "fill", selector: string, value: string } | { kind: "click", selector: string, expectBackend?: { op?: "backend.invoke" | "backend.attempt" | "backend.upload" | "backend.file" | "backend.external" | "collection.list" | "collection.create" | "host.copy" | "host.print" | "host.notice" | "unknown", operation?: string, status?: integer, refusalCode?: string } })[], timeoutMs?: integer } | { action: "createLink", workspaceId?: string, appRoot: string, paths?: string[], access?: "view" | "comment" | "edit", operationId: UUID, agentLabel?: string } | { action: "personalFolder", workspaceId?: string, open?: boolean } | { action: "listLocal", workspaceId?: string, appRoot: string, versionId?: string } | { action: "checkLocal", workspaceId?: string, appRoot: string, versionId?: string } | { action: "prepareLocal", workspaceId?: string, appRoot: string, versionId?: string } | { action: "stage", workspaceId?: string, appRoot: string, migrations?: { [key: string]: string }, agentLabel?: string } | { action: "listStaged", workspaceId?: string, appRoot?: string } | { action: "approveStaged", workspaceId?: string, stageId: UUID, reviewDigest: SHA-256 hex, agentLabel?: string } | { action: "discardStaged", workspaceId?: string, stageId: UUID } | { action: "launchLocal", workspaceId?: string, publicationId: SHA-256 hex } | { action: "list", workspaceId?: string, appRoot: string, cursor?: SHA-256 hex } | { action: "prepare", workspaceId?: string, appRoot: string, audience?: "workspace", shareId?: string, grantId?: string } | { action: "approve", workspaceId?: string, approvalId: UUID, candidateDigest: SHA-256 hex, agentLabel?: string, linkReads?: ({ operationId: UUID, fieldIds: UUID[] })[] } | { action: "cancel", workspaceId?: string, approvalId: UUID } | { action: "withdraw", workspaceId?: string, publicationId: SHA-256 hex, expectedAuthorityRevision: integer } | { action: "revokeCollection", workspaceId?: string, publicationId: SHA-256 hex, expectedAuthorityRevision: integer } | { action: "reviewReactivation", workspaceId?: string, publicationId: SHA-256 hex }`. Required.

Returns the requested action's result, listed under [`dohc app`](#dohc-app). Only `createLink` returns a bearer link `url` once, in `linkCreated`. `urlUnavailable` includes `grantId` so the owner can end it in dohc. Shared approval returns `published` with `appQuery` (`?app=<publicationId>`), never the link URL. An app for members returns no `appQuery`. Append `appQuery` before the fragment of any link URL, including one returned by `createLink`. Keep the link secret yourself.

### `dohc_import_data`

Import a CSV/JSON/JSONL/Markdown source into a new visible .sqlite database. Requires dohc open and records the write under your agent name.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `sourcePath`: `string`. Required.
- `databasePath`: `string`. Required.
- `tableName`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, tableName, rowCount }`.

### `dohc_query_database`

Run a single read-only SELECT against a visible workspace database (bounded rows).

- `databasePath`: `string`. Required.
- `sql`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, rows }`, with at most 1,000 rows.

### `dohc_list_notices`

List the Notices rows for this workspace, newest first. Each row has its title, text, sender, time, whether it is read, and where it opens (`opens`): a file or folder path, a chat thread and message to read with dohc_read_chat, or an automation. A row with nowhere to go has `opens: null`, and `note` says why when dohc knows. Listing does not change whether rows are read.

No arguments.

Returns `{ notices: { kind, id, title, body, sender, createdAtMs, read, opens, note? }[] }`.

### `dohc_inbox_list`

List items in the workspace's Inbox Collection (Inbox/). Returns exists: false without creating Inbox/ when none exists yet. Optionally filter by status (New, Filed, Archived).

The workspace Inbox belongs to the owning workspace. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `status`: `"New" | "Filed" | "Archived"`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ exists, items: { kind, id, path, title, status, source, received, url?, attachment?, filedTo? }[], hasMore }`.

### `dohc_inbox_add`

Capture a note or link into the owning workspace's Inbox Collection (Inbox/). Creates Inbox/collection.yaml lazily on first capture and writes a Markdown record with safe YAML frontmatter.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `title`: `string`
- `body`: `string`
- `url`: `string`
- `kind`: `"note" | "file" | "image" | "link" | "webhook"`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, recordId, title, createdInbox } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_inbox_archive`

Mark a record in Inbox/ as Archived by updating its Status field through its live document session. Returns the previous Status so the change can be reversed.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `item`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, previousStatus, changed } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_inbox_move`

Move an Inbox Markdown record (and any linked attachments under Inbox/files/) into an owned workspace folder outside Inbox/. Rewrites workspace links and returns History operation id(s) that can be undone.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `item`: `string`. Required.
- `targetFolder`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, fromPath, toPath, operationId?, attachments: { fromPath, toPath, operationId? }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

---

**Workspace files and links.** Read, write, search, organize ordinary workspace files, and inspect document links.

### `dohc_list_files`

List visible files and folders in the workspace. Hidden dohc internals are omitted.

- `path`: `string`
- `recursive`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, root, entries: { path, kind, bytes?, mediaType? }[] }`.

### `dohc_read_file`

Read any visible workspace file as UTF-8 text or base64, returning size and sha256 for safe follow-up writes. A shared note's Markdown file can trail the note while its edits wait for the server, even when the result carries no warning; dohc_workspace_status lists those notes as pendingShare, and dohc_read_document returns their current text.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `encoding`: `"utf8" | "base64"`
- `maxBytes`: `integer`
- `offsetBytes`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, mediaType, encoding, bytes, offsetBytes, sha256, truncated, content, warning? }`. `warning` is present when the file is a shared note whose edits wait for the server, so the file holds older text than the note. `content` is always the file's bytes. No `warning` does not mean the file is current: it is left out when the dohc app does not answer within 50 ms.

### `dohc_search_files`

Search visible workspace file paths and text contents. Hidden dohc internals, .git, node_modules, symlinks, oversized files, and binary files are skipped.

- `query`: `string`. Required.
- `path`: `string`
- `mode`: `"content" | "path" | "both"`
- `caseSensitive`: `boolean`
- `regex`: `boolean`
- `maxResults`: `integer`
- `maxFileBytes`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, query, root, mode, matches: { type, path, mediaType?, line?, column?, preview }[], matchCount, limitHit, skipped: { path, reason }[] }`.

### `dohc_write_file`

Write an ordinary workspace file. Markdown documents are created with dohc_create_document and changed with dohc_edit_document, and .excalidraw drawings with dohc_create_drawing and dohc_edit_drawing; this tool refuses both. Requires dohc open. History records the write under your agent name. Refuses secret or excluded paths and content over 10 MiB.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `content`: `string`. Required.
- `encoding`: `"utf8" | "base64"`
- `expectedSha256`: `string`
- `summary`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, bytes, sha256 }`. Uses the desktop `fileWrite` verb. On failure: `{ ok: false, reason, written?, path?, currentSha256? }`. `written` lists published files in a partial batch.

### `dohc_create_directory`

Create a visible workspace directory. Files later written inside it are captured as engine moments by the desktop watcher.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `summary`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path }`, or `{ ok: true, path, unchanged: true }` when the folder exists.

### `dohc_duplicate_file`

Duplicate one regular file beside its source with a fresh identity. Owner workspace only. Undo removes the copy while it is unchanged.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, operationId, undo: { available: true } | { available: false, reason, paths }, path, materialized } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_move_path`

Move or rename a visible workspace file or folder. Returns operationId and undo availability. Use dohc_undo_operation when available. Overwrites, moves that change only letter case, and files without History rows update no links. A folder move updates no links. Other file moves update [[links]] after the result returns. dohc_read_operation lists the documents it could not update. Requires dohc open. History records the move under your agent name. Refuses links, and secret, excluded, or reserved paths, including any inside a folder. Files over 5 MiB binary or 10 MiB text move without a History row. Text with invalid UTF-8 also moves without a row when History cannot keep it as binary. `withoutHistory` lists their destination paths. With overwrite, `replaced` separately reports the old destination's trash location and files without History copies. A failed move puts everything back it can. `deleted` lists files History records as deleted after rollback. They stay in the workspace's .dohc/local/trash, and Restore in History brings them back. In a version other than Main, refuses to change files the version does not track, such as files over those sizes, because they have one copy for every version and the change also happens in Main. Set confirmNotVersioned to true to change them anyway.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `fromPath`: `string`. Required.
- `toPath`: `string`. Required.
- `overwrite`: `boolean`
- `confirmNotVersioned`: `boolean`
- `summary`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, operationId, fromPath, toPath, withoutHistory?, replaced? }`. Uses the desktop `fileMove` verb. `withoutHistory` lists moved files with no History row: oversized files or non-UTF-8 text that History cannot keep as binary. `replaced` describes the old destination separately: `{ path, trashed, trashPath?, withoutHistory }`. `trashed` is true when the system trash took it; otherwise `trashPath` names its workspace trash entry. `replaced.withoutHistory` lists replaced files without History copies; other replaced files can be restored in History. On failure: `{ ok: false, reason, path?, deleted?, withoutHistory?, replaced? }`. The reason reports rollback's outcome. `withoutHistory` names moved files without History rows after rollback. `replaced` reports any old destination files retained in the workspace trash. `deleted` lists files History records as deleted after the failed move. They stay in the workspace's .dohc/local/trash.

### `dohc_delete_path`

Delete a visible workspace file or folder. Returns operationId and undo availability. Use dohc_undo_operation when available. Requires dohc open. History records the delete under your agent name, and Restore there brings the file back. Files over 5 MiB binary or 10 MiB text delete without a History row. Text with invalid UTF-8 also deletes without a row when History cannot keep it as binary. `withoutHistory` lists their paths. Restore these files from the trash. The file or folder goes through the workspace's .dohc/local/trash to the system trash, or stays in .dohc/local/trash when the system refuses; `trashed` says which. Refuses links, and secret, excluded, or reserved paths, including any inside a folder. If History refuses a file in a folder, `deleted` lists the files already deleted, and the rest go back to their place. In a version other than Main, refuses to change files the version does not track, such as files over those sizes, because they have one copy for every version and the change also happens in Main. Set confirmNotVersioned to true to change them anyway.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `confirmNotVersioned`: `boolean`
- `summary`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, operationId, undo, path, trashed, trashPath?, withoutHistory? }`. Uses the desktop `fileDelete` verb. `trashed` is true when the system trash took the entry; otherwise `trashPath` names its workspace trash entry. `withoutHistory` lists files deleted without History rows: oversized files or non-UTF-8 text that History cannot keep as binary. On failure: `{ ok: false, reason, deleted?, path?, withoutHistory? }`. `deleted` lists files History recorded as deleted before it refused `path`. `withoutHistory` names files already removed without History rows. The reason names their workspace trash location.

### `dohc_link`

Make a link to a chat, thread, message, file, app, or Collection. Pass exactly one of `group` (a Group, DM, or agent chat, by name, #slug, or id), `thread`, `message` (ids), or `path` (a file, or an app or a Collection by its folder). Put the returned `link` text, `@[work:...]`, in a chat message: it shows as a chip that opens what it names, and keeps working after a rename or move.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `group`: `string`
- `thread`: `string`
- `message`: `string`
- `path`: `string`

Returns `{ kind, reference, link }`.

### `dohc_links_connections`

Read how the workspace's Collections, Datasets, apps, automations, and Groups connect, from files on this computer. approval says whether an app's data access is approved on this computer or only requested in app.publish.json. records lists each Collection's record files. complete is false when the answer was cut to fit 64 KiB. A received share lists only its shared Collections, their records, and Relations between them. An ended share, a joined workspace, or a call from inside shared-with-me returns scope share-omitted with nothing listed.

No arguments.

Returns `{ scope, nodes: ({ kind: "document-collection", id, title, path, recordCount } | { kind: "dataset", id, title, path, datasetId, firstTableId } | { kind: "app", id, title, path, entryPath } | { kind: "automation", id, title, path, automationId, enabled } | { kind: "group", id, title, channelId })[], edges: { kind, source, target, approval? }[], records: { collection, paths }[], complete, mountsCovered }`.

### `dohc_links_edges`

Read a bounded page of file links and isolated Markdown files and drawings. Continue nextCursor until null. indexBuilding reports active indexing; unchecked names uncertified sources; mountsCovered reports mount coverage.

- `cursor`: `string`

Returns `{ versionId, files: { objectId, path, title }[], entries: { kind, source, target, ordinal }[], unchecked, complete, indexBuilding, mountsCovered, nextCursor }`.

### `dohc_links_in`

Read a bounded page of documents linking to a file. indexBuilding reports active indexing; unchecked names omitted sources. complete excludes mount coverage, reported by mountsCovered. Cursors carry index state across pages.

- `subject`: `{ path: string } | { objectId: string }`. Required.
- `cursor`: `string`

Returns `{ versionId, subject: { path, objectId }, entries: { source, title, ordinal, span, line, highlightStart, highlightEnd, snippet }[], unchecked, complete, indexBuilding, mountsCovered, nextCursor } | null`.

### `dohc_links_resolve`

Resolve wikilink or Markdown literals from one source document using the engine's link rules.

- `source`: `string`. Required.
- `literals`: `({ kind: "wikilink" | "markdown", literal: string })[]`. Required.

Returns `{ versionId, results: ({ path, fragment } | { path, create, fragment } | null)[], mountsCovered }`.

---

**Chat and Groups.** Read Groups and threads, post updates or polls, comment on files, and watch for replies.

### `dohc_list_groups`

List the workspace's Chats groups (including the default #general) with each group's chats and their ids. It also returns direct messages and the agent lane, told apart by `kind`. Requires the workspace engine.

No arguments.

Returns `{ ok: true, groups: { kind, id, channelWireId?, name, slug, purpose?, threadCount, threads }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_create_group`

Create a Chats group and its folder, as New group does. `name` is the group's name, 1 to 80 characters with a letter or number; its folder is the name as a slug. `purpose` says what the group is for. `type` is posts, chat, or both, the default. `level` sets what members can do in it as it is made: comment lets them post, view lets them read, none hides it from them. A group made with a level has no folder, and needs a connection. A name already taken is refused; find that group with dohc_list_groups. Returns the group's id, name, slug, and kind for dohc_start_group_chat.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `name`: `string`. Required.
- `purpose`: `string`
- `type`: `"posts" | "chat" | "both"`
- `level`: `"comment" | "view" | "none"`

Returns `{ ok: true, group: { id, name, slug, kind, purpose? } }`.

### `dohc_read_chat`

Read one dohc Chat thread, or one group's stream. With `threadId`: its messages (with author kind, display name, and the product, version, and model an agent reported, in `authorReported`), whether agent replies are paused and the latest run outcome, and a read-only text projection. With `group` (a name, #slug, or id): its posts and conversation messages in one order, oldest first, a page at a time from the newest end. Each post says how many replies it has, who replied, and the latest agent reply. A message an agent reported work with has `work`, and a post whose thread has such a report has its Work card in `post.work`. Pass `nextBefore` back as `before` for the older page; `limit` is 50 by default, at most 100. Messages name the agents still asked to answer them in `agentRequests`.

- `threadId`: `string`
- `group`: `string`
- `before`: `{ createdAtMs: integer, lane: "posts" | "chat", id: string }`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, thread: { id, title, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, linkedPathHint? }, dispatch: { paused, lastRun }, messages: { id, threadId, authorKind, authorDisplayName, authorOwnerDisplayName?, body, createdAtMs, parentMessageId?, attachments, needsDecision, decisionState?, options?, optionDetails?, chosenOption?, resolvedByMessageId?, reactions?, agentRequests?, authorReported?, work? }[], projection: { path, readOnly: true, text } } | { ok: true, stream: { group, items, nextBefore, readPosition } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_start_group_chat`

Start a new chat in a group as the agent. `group` accepts a group name, #slug, or id. No title needed; the chat displays its first message. `attachments` name tracked files relative to the MCP server folder; `needsDecision` asks for a decision and `options` turns it into a poll: give each choice as a short label, or as `{ label, detail }` with a one-line explanation, and keep the choices out of `body` so people read them once; `runId` links the message to a local agent run. `model` names the model you run as, such as Claude Opus 5.5; people see it marked as reported, beside the product and version your MCP client reports. Leave it out if you don't know. `work` reports work you do outside dohc, such as a thread in another product or a pull request: `status` is working, waiting, done, failed, or stopped, and `url` is an http or https link to the work, in plain ASCII with other characters percent-encoded. The chat then shows a Work card with the status and link of its newest report, marked as reported. Reply with `work` again to change it, and give `url` again to keep the link. Returns engine ids usable with dohc_read_chat.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `group`: `string`. Required.
- `title`: `string`
- `body`: `string`. Required.
- `attachments`: `string[]`
- `needsDecision`: `boolean`
- `options`: `(string | { label: string, detail?: string })[]`
- `runId`: `string`
- `model`: `string`
- `work`: `{ status: "working" | "waiting" | "done" | "failed" | "stopped", url?: string }`

Returns `{ ok: true, group: { id, slug, kind }, threadId, messageId, title, warning? }`.

### `dohc_reply_to_chat`

Reply in a dohc Chat thread as the agent. `to` replies under one message; `resolve` closes that open decision with this reply and `choose` names the option picked. Message ids come from dohc_read_chat. `attachments`, `needsDecision`, `options`, `runId`, `model`, and `work` behave as in dohc_start_group_chat. A run an automation started that has nothing to report sends `nothingToReport: true` with only `threadId` and `runId`, and no `body`: it posts nothing, and the run ends without a failure.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `threadId`: `string`. Required.
- `to`: `string`
- `resolve`: `string`
- `choose`: `string`
- `body`: `string`
- `attachments`: `string[]`
- `needsDecision`: `boolean`
- `options`: `(string | { label: string, detail?: string })[]`
- `runId`: `string`
- `model`: `string`
- `work`: `{ status: "working" | "waiting" | "done" | "failed" | "stopped", url?: string }`
- `nothingToReport`: `true`

Returns `{ ok: true, threadId, messageId, parentMessageId?, resolvedMessageId?, warning? }`, or `{ ok: true, threadId, nothingToReport: true }`.

### `dohc_list_file_chats`

List the dohc Chats linked to a workspace file. Chats follow the file's stable dohc identity across renames. Requires the workspace engine.

- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, fileObjectId, threads: { id, title, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, linkedPathHint? }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_start_file_chat`

Comment on a workspace file as the agent. This starts a chat linked to the file, as a person does from the file's Chats panel: `title` names the chat there and `body` is its first message. dohc_list_file_chats returns it, and dohc_reply_to_chat continues it. `requestId` is a random key you choose, such as a UUID. Sent again with the same key, after a timeout for example, the comment returns its first result instead of starting a second chat, while it runs and until 1,024 later keyed requests to this workspace have finished. dohc then refuses the key until 16,384 more have finished; after that, or after dohc restarts, the key can start another chat. `runId` and `model` behave as in dohc_start_group_chat. To comment on a passage of a Markdown file, start `body` with a Markdown quote of the passage (`> the passage`), then a blank line, then the comment: the file's editor highlights that passage and opens the comment from it.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `title`: `string`. Required.
- `body`: `string`. Required.
- `requestId`: `string`
- `runId`: `string`
- `model`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, threadId, messageId, warning? } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_wait_for_messages`

Wait for this agent's unread requests without marking them read. In a run dohc started, they are the run's own requests, including replies in threads its agent posted in, and the ones it returns start no new run. With --agent-id, they are that agent's: its direct messages, messages that @ its name, and replies in threads it posted in. Otherwise, they are @agent mentions and replies in threads an agent with no id posted in. Returns messages and a cursor, or an empty batch after at most 25 seconds. Call in a loop with the returned cursor and the same filters. Group and thread filters only narrow the inbox. At most 4 waits can run on this connection.

The agent inbox belongs to the owning workspace. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `cursor`: `string`
- `group`: `string`
- `thread`: `string`
- `timeoutMs`: `integer`

Returns `{ messages: { threadId, messageId, group, author, createdAtMs, text }[], cursor }`.

### `dohc_retry_chat_run`

Run an agent's stopped request in a dohc Chat thread again, as Try again does under its message. dohc_read_chat reports a stopped run under dispatch.lastRun. Each request gets two attempts. Only the computer that ran it can run it again, and only for someone who may post in the thread.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `threadId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, status: "queued", threadId } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_chat_links`

Read one bounded page of accessible files mentioned in a chat. Use channelWireId from dohc_list_groups, and continue nextCursor until null. Coverage can be partial.

- `channelWireId`: `string`. Required.
- `cursor`: `string`

Returns `{ versionId, subject: { channelWireId }, unchecked, complete, indexBuilding, mountsCovered, sharedChannelRowsUncovered, nextCursor, entries: { threadId, messageId, mentionedAtMs, file, author }[] } | null`.

### `dohc_chat_file_mentions`

Read a bounded page of accessible chat mentions of files. Optional subject selects one file. Continue nextCursor until null; complete and sharedChannelRowsUncovered report coverage.

- `subject`: `{ path: string } | { objectId: string }`
- `cursor`: `string`

Returns `{ versionId, subject: { objectId, path } | null, entries: { attachment, message, thread, channelId?, channelWireId?, channelName?, channelSlug?, channelKind? }[], unchecked, complete, indexBuilding, mountsCovered, sharedChannelRowsUncovered, nextCursor } | null`.

---

**Automations and Buttons.** Inspect Collection automations, toggle them, press Button fields, check run logs, move automations to the server, and create incoming webhooks.

### `dohc_list_automations`

Read automation definitions and on/off file state in a Collection, including shares. Shared run history and host runtime are unavailable.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, definitions } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_switch_automation`

Change only one automation's enabled value. Read definitions first and provide their contentHash. Reformat confirms losing comments and hand formatting. After an unknown desktop save, read definitions and sync state before retrying; a stale base remains a conflict. A pending save is waiting to sync; acceptance records history, not host execution.

Available only in a shared workspace with edit access.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `automation`: `string`. Required.
- `enabled`: `boolean`. Required.
- `expectedContentHash`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `reformat`: `boolean`
- `submitId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, result } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_inspect_buttons`

Inspect a Collection's Button fields, their current access, and any actions that need confirmation. Shared Collection buttons are checked on the owner's host.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `table`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, buttons: { field, table?, state }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_press_button`

Press a Button field on one record, as a person clicks it in dohc, and get the id of the run it started; follow it with dohc_read_automation_run. Name the record by its id, or a dataset record by its primary key as JSON. A press that would run actions dohc cannot undo is refused with each action's name; press again with those names in confirm to run them. Send the same requestId again, after a timeout for example, to get the same press instead of a second one. The press is recorded as the agent's, for the person; from an agent run that an automation started, it counts in that chain of automations, which stops after 4 steps.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `button`: `string`. Required.
- `recordId`: `string`. Required.
- `table`: `string`
- `confirm`: `string[]`
- `requestId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, run, outcome, error, waiting } | { ok: true, relayed: true } | { ok: false, reason, confirm: { name, label }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_automation_runs`

List an automation's runs on this computer, 20 at a time, newest first: each run's id, state, what started it, how many changes it made, and why it failed. Name the automation by its Collection's folder and its id in automations.yaml. When older runs remain, `next` is not null; pass it as `page` to list them. Each computer keeps the runs of the automations it ran for 30 days after they end. With server true, list the runs of the workspace's self-hosted server instead. A run marked unsentChangesLost ran in a copy the server lost, and its latest changes may not have been sent.

A shared view keeps no automation runs, so it does not offer this tool.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `automation`: `string`. Required.
- `page`: `string`
- `server`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, runs: { run, state, error, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, trigger, definitionChanged, neverStarted, chainStopped, undone, unsentChangesLost?: true, changes }[], next } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_automation_run`

Read one automation run: what started it, what each step changed, why it failed, which step failed, and whether Try again resumes there or starts over. Steps count from 1 in the order automations.yaml lists them, including the steps inside if and otherwise. A step that changed nothing is not listed. With server true, read a run of the workspace's self-hosted server: it lists what the run changed, oldest first, as `changes` instead of steps.

A shared view keeps no automation runs, so it does not offer this tool.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `automation`: `string`. Required.
- `run`: `string`. Required.
- `server`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, run: { run, state, error, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, trigger, definitionChanged, neverStarted, chainStopped, undone, unsentChangesLost?: true, findMs?, planMs?, writeMs?, writeCount?, steps, failedStep, startsOver } | { run, state, error, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, trigger, definitionChanged, neverStarted, chainStopped, undone, unsentChangesLost?: true, server: true, changes } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_retry_automation_run`

Try a failed automation run again, as Try again does in dohc. It resumes after the last step that finished. If the automation changed since the run failed, it refuses unless startOver is true, which runs it from the first step and can repeat changes the run already made. Only the computer that ran it can try a run again; anywhere else the refusal names that computer.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `automation`: `string`. Required.
- `run`: `string`. Required.
- `startOver`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, status: "queued" } | { ok: false, status: "switched-off", reason, target: { recovery: "automation-controls", automation, path } } | { ok: false, status: "definition-changed", repeatsMessages, repeatsWebhooks?, reason } | { ok: false, reason, notice?: { title, body } }`.

### `dohc_read_automation_host`

Read which of the owner's computers, or the dohc server, runs this workspace's automations and schedules. kind relay gives the generation that dohc_use_server_for_automations needs, the host's installId (server for the dohc server), and handoverFrom while a computer hands over.

Only the owner's own agents set up the workspace. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

No arguments.

Returns `{ kind: "this-computer" } | { kind: "another-computer", label, sameName, waits } | { kind: "no-computer", message, cause? } | { kind: "none" } | { kind: "note", message } | { kind: "relay", generation, hostInstallId, handoverFrom, computers: { kind, installId, label, lastSeenMs, thisComputer }[] }`.

### `dohc_use_server_for_automations`

Move a synced workspace's automations and schedules to the dohc server, so they run while the owner's computers are off. Pass the generation from dohc_read_automation_host. moved means the server runs them now. handover-pending names the computer that must release them first; if it stays offline, the owner uses Take over in Settings › Advanced. A stale generation is refused: read the host again.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `generation`: `integer`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, outcome, generation, handoverFrom } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_incoming_webhooks`

List this workspace's incoming webhooks: each one's name, Collection, paused state, and recent deliveries. Never returns their addresses. List before you retry a create whose result you don't know.

Only the owner's own agents set up the workspace. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

No arguments.

Returns `{ kind: "none" } | { kind: "unavailable", message } | { kind: "ready", serverOrigin, webhooks: { webhookId, name, collectionPath, collectionId, paused, pauseReason, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, lastDeliveryAtMs, pendingCount, recentDeliveries }[], limit }`.

### `dohc_create_incoming_webhook`

Create an incoming webhook for a private Collection in a synced workspace the person you work for owns. collection is the Collection's folder, relative to the workspace root. Returns the address once, as endpointUrl. It is a secret: anyone who has it can add records, so give it only to the person you work for or the site that posts to it. If you don't know whether a create worked, list incoming webhooks before you try again. Creating needs the server to run the workspace's automations (dohc_use_server_for_automations) with no handover waiting. The owner deletes or rotates it in Settings › Secrets › Incoming webhooks.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `name`: `string`. Required.
- `collection`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, webhook: { webhookId, name, collectionPath, collectionId, paused, pauseReason, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, lastDeliveryAtMs, pendingCount, recentDeliveries }, endpointUrl } | { ok: false, reason }`.

---

**Versions and History.** Work in parallel workspace Versions, resolve merge conflicts, and inspect or undo History.

### `dohc_list_versions`

List the workspace's versions and which one is active. Archived versions are hidden unless includeArchived is true. canMergeIntoMain is true for a version that started from Main. A version's madeFromVersionId is the id of the version it was made from. Owner workspace only.

A shared view keeps no versions of its own, so it does not offer this tool.

- `includeArchived`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, versions: { kind, id, name, createdAtMs, canMergeIntoMain, madeFromVersionId?, archivedAtMs? }[], activeVersionId } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_create_version`

Create a version from the active one and switch the workspace folder to it. The new version starts as a copy. Refuses a name another version has. First saves the edits open in dohc, and refuses when it can't. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `name`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, version: { id, name } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_switch_version`

Switch the workspace folder to a version, named by its name or id from dohc_list_versions. dohc first saves the active version's files and the edits open in dohc, and refuses when it can't. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `version`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, version: { id, name }, changedFileCount } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_compare_version`

Read one page of files that differ between a version and Main. Name the version by its name or id from dohc_list_versions. currentText is Main's text and incomingText the version's; binary files carry no text. Files History does not track and secret files are left out. Continue with afterPath set to nextAfterPath until it is null. Owner workspace only.

A shared view keeps no versions of its own, so it does not offer this tool.

- `version`: `string`. Required.
- `afterPath`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, version: { id, name }, files: { path, status, currentText?, incomingText?, binary? }[], nextAfterPath } | { ok: false, reason } | { ok: false, status: "policy-unreadable", unreadable, reason }`.

### `dohc_merge_version`

Merge a version into Main, named by its name or id from dohc_list_versions. Only versions made from Main can merge into Main. Returns the merged and conflict counts and the first page of open conflicts, as dohc_list_version_conflicts does. First saves the edits open in dohc, and refuses when it can't. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `version`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, version: { id, name }, mergedFileCount, unchangedFileCount, conflictCount, conflicts: { conflictId, path, sourceVersionId, targetVersionId, origin, contentKind, currentText, incomingText, baseText, currentBinary?, incomingBinary?, baseBinary?, waiting? }[], nextAfterConflictId } | { ok: false, reason } | { ok: false, status: "policy-unreadable", unreadable, reason }`.

### `dohc_update_version`

Bring Main's changes into a version made from Main, named by its name or id from dohc_list_versions. Returns the merged and conflict counts, the count of protected files both sides changed (left as the version has them), and the first page of open conflicts. In an update's conflicts, current is the version and incoming is Main. First saves the edits open in dohc, and refuses when it can't. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `version`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, version: { id, name }, mergedFileCount, unchangedFileCount, conflictCount, conflicts: { conflictId, path, sourceVersionId, targetVersionId, origin, contentKind, currentText, incomingText, baseText, currentBinary?, incomingBinary?, baseBinary?, waiting? }[], nextAfterConflictId, skippedProtectedFileCount } | { ok: false, reason } | { ok: false, status: "policy-unreadable", unreadable, reason }`.

### `dohc_archive_version`

Archive a version, named by its name or id from dohc_list_versions, or restore it with restore: true. An archived version keeps its files, leaves the version menu, and can't be switched to or merged until restored. Main, the active version, and versions with open conflicts can't be archived. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `version`: `string`. Required.
- `restore`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, version: { id, name }, archived } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_version_conflicts`

Read one page of open conflicts from merges and from sync, with each side's text. origin sync means two computers changed the file; waiting says another computer's newer version waits until that conflict is resolved. Files History does not track are left out. Continue with afterConflictId set to nextAfterConflictId until it is null. Owner workspace only.

A shared view keeps no versions of its own, so it does not offer this tool.

- `afterConflictId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, conflicts: { conflictId, path, sourceVersionId, targetVersionId, origin, contentKind, currentText, incomingText, baseText, currentBinary?, incomingBinary?, baseBinary?, waiting? }[], nextAfterConflictId } | { ok: false, reason } | { ok: false, status: "policy-unreadable", unreadable, reason }`.

### `dohc_resolve_version_conflict`

Resolve an open conflict from dohc_list_version_conflicts. keep current or incoming keeps that side; keep combined with text replaces both. In a merge, current is Main and incoming is the version; in an update, current is the version and incoming is Main; in sync, current is this computer. A binary conflict takes no combined text. Returns the open conflicts that remain. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `conflictId`: `string`. Required.
- `resolution`: `{ keep: "current" | "incoming" } | { keep: "combined", text: string }`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, conflicts: { conflictId, path, sourceVersionId, targetVersionId, origin, contentKind, currentText, incomingText, baseText, currentBinary?, incomingBinary?, baseBinary?, waiting? }[], nextAfterConflictId } | { ok: false, reason } | { ok: false, status: "policy-unreadable", unreadable, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_changes`

List workspace history, newest first: workspace-engine moments (the recorder for this workspace). Each entry carries path/operation/versionId. Pass path, relative to the MCP server folder, to list only that file's changes across its renames.

- `sinceMs`: `integer`
- `limit`: `integer`
- `includeFiles`: `boolean`
- `path`: `string`

Returns `{ changes: { operationId?, id, recordedAtMs, source: "workspace-engine", operation, path, versionId, authors?, fileCount: 1, files? }[], count, totalAvailable, hasMore, cursorMs } | { ok: false, status: "policy-unreadable", unreadable, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_change`

Read one history entry by id: a workspace-engine moment with its full before/after payload.

- `id`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, change: { operationId?, id, recordedAtMs, source: "workspace-engine", operation, path, versionId, authors?, fileCount: 1, files, before, after } } | { ok: false, reason } | { ok: false, status: "untracked", reason } | { ok: false, status: "policy-unreadable", unreadable, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_operation`

List the paths changed by one operation, up to 50 per page. Returns change references and paths without retained contents, and a file move's link update state. Owner workspace only.

Operation reads require the owning workspace. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `operationId`: `string`. Required.
- `cursor`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: false, reason } | { ok: true, operationId, members: { momentId, operation, path, beforePath? }[], withoutHistory?, links?: { state: "updating" } | { state: "done", documents, unchecked, uncheckedCount }, nextCursor }`.

### `dohc_undo_operation`

Undo a delete, move, or rename by its operation id. Requires dohc open and the owning workspace. Returns History restoration state, restored paths, and remaining paths with reasons and retry flags. Undo again to retry each remaining path marked retry. Undo of a move also reverses its link updates.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `operationId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: false, reason, refusal: { code: "old-path-occupied", path } | { code: "live-page-owned", path } | { code: "unexplained" } } | { ok: true, tracked: { state, momentCount }, restored, remaining: { path, reason, retry }[] }`.

### `dohc_plan_agent_run_undo`

Inspect which files saved during one agent run can be safely restored to before the run, and which files would be skipped because of later edits, renames, path collisions, live editing, or protection.

Only the original workspace plans an agent run undo. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `agentRunId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ agentRunId, agentName, planToken, truncated, scannedChanges, restorable: { action, objectId, path, earliestMomentId, latestMomentId, momentCount }[], skipped: { path, reason, detail }[], policyUnreadable? }`.

---

**Sharing and connected agents.** Inspect owned share codes, manage agents connected through a share link, manage the workspace's members, and share and review Member apps.

### `dohc_read_share_copy`

Read one owned grant's share code and named-account invite link. Requires the original workspace and its signed-in owner account. Ended grants return only status; unknown and link grants are refused.

The code and invite link belong to the owner's sharing. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `shareId`: `string`. Required.
- `grantId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ status: "active", shareCode, browserInvitationUrl? } | { status: "ended" }`.

### `dohc_list_link_agents`

List the agents signed in through one share link, 50 a page. Requires the original workspace and its signed-in owner account. Find the link's shareId and grantId with `dohc access sharing granted`. reportedName is the name the agent's client reported; dohc cannot check it. Pass nextCursor as cursor until it is null.

A link's agents belong to the owner's sharing. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `shareId`: `string`. Required.
- `grantId`: `string`. Required.
- `cursor`: `string`

Returns `{ agents: { connectionId, reportedName, connectedAtMs, lastActionAtMs }[], nextCursor }`.

### `dohc_disconnect_link_agent`

End one agent's connection through a share link. The link and its other agents keep working. Requires the original workspace and its signed-in owner account. Find connectionId with dohc_list_link_agents.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `shareId`: `string`. Required.
- `grantId`: `string`. Required.
- `connectionId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ connectionId }`.

### `dohc_members`

Do what the Members page does, in a workspace you own or joined: list people, invites, and removed accounts; invite by email (dohc emails them an invitation when the server sends email, and inviting the same address again emails it again; they join when they sign in to dohc with that address); remove someone; let a removed account back in; make someone an admin or a member; set what members can do (view, comment, or edit); show or set what members can do in one Group (group is a Group name or id; level comment lets them post, view lets them read, none hides the Group, null removes the Group's own access so it takes the member level; leave level out to read it); set or clear folder access (folder with change containing a workspace-relative folder and members plus people, or clear: true; use ruleId and revision from list to target a specific rule; members null hides the folder; people are email and level pairs); remove an unknown marker (folderMarker with folder); turn the invite link on or off or reset it; end membership for everyone; or delete a message in a Group or a file's Comments (deleteMessage, with its threadId and messageId). The server decides what your role allows: members see names and roles and delete their own messages; admins also invite, remove members, let them back in, set the level and folder or Group access, manage the invite link, and delete any message in a Group or Comments; only the owner changes roles or ends membership. A person is a memberId from list, or an email. Removing someone or ending membership ends their access; copies already on their computers stay. Deleting a message can't be undone. It shows as deleted everywhere it syncs, but people who already read it may keep a copy. Ask the person you work for before you remove anyone, hide a Group, narrow folder access, end membership, or delete someone else's message.

- `request`: `{ action: "list" } | { action: "invite", email: string } | { action: "level", level: "view" | "comment" | "edit" } | { action: "role", person: string, role: "admin" | "member" } | { action: "remove", person: string } | { action: "letBackIn", person: string } | { action: "link", change: "turn-on" | "turn-off" | "reset" } | { action: "end" } | { action: "group", group: string, level?: "comment" | "view" | "none" | null } | { action: "deleteMessage", threadId: string, messageId: string } | { action: "folder", change: { folder: string, members: "view" | "comment" | "edit" | null, people: ({ email: string, level: "view" | "comment" | "edit" })[], create?: true } | { ruleId: string, revision: integer, members: "view" | "comment" | "edit" | null, people: ({ email: string, level: "view" | "comment" | "edit" })[] } | { folder: string, clear: true } | { ruleId: string, revision: integer, clear: true } } | { action: "folderMarker", folder: string }`. Required.

Returns `{ status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } } | { status: "refused" } | { status: "done" } | { status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

### `dohc_collection_access`

As an Admin of a workspace you joined, read a Collection and manage its access and rules on the workspace's server. Address it with datasetPath, its dataset.json path relative to the MCP server folder. list and describe show every Collection on the server with the reads the Owner has. invoke runs a read operation with its described revision and a stable retry key; a write needs a grant that holds it. permissions lists per-person grants, the workspace defaults, and rules: the approved revision, revisionSha256, and the actions grants and defaults may hold. setDefaults sets the actions each member level holds (view, comment, edit), named under that revision; View and Comment hold only read-only actions. setGrant and removeGrant change one person's grant. create makes a new Collection from a dataset.json definition and approves it as you. prepareSchemaChange and prepareMigration prepare a rules change for review, migrationPreviewPage reads more of the records it changes, and approveMigration or discardMigration ends the review. approval says who approved the rules the Collection runs. The server refuses anyone who is not an Admin, and a Collection kept on the Owner's computer. Ask the person you work for before you narrow anyone's access or approve a rules change.

Available only in a shared workspace with view or comment or edit access.

- `request`: `{ workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, action: "permissions", after?: string, limit?: integer } | { workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, action: "setGrant", grantId: string, grant: { revision: integer, revisionSha256: SHA-256 hex, operationIds: UUID[], discover: boolean } } | { workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, action: "setDefaults", defaults: { view: UUID[], comment: UUID[], edit: UUID[], revision: integer, revisionSha256: SHA-256 hex } } | { workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, action: "removeGrant", principalKey: string } | { workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, action: "approval" } | { workspaceId?: string, action: "list", after?: UUID, limit?: integer, includeArchived?: boolean } | { workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, action: "describe", includeArchived?: boolean } | { workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, action: "invoke", operationId: UUID, revision: integer, revisionSha256: SHA-256 hex, input: any JSON, idempotencyKey: string, invocationId?: UUID } | { workspaceId?: string, action: "create", definition: any JSON } | { workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, revision: integer, revisionSha256: SHA-256 hex, action: "prepareSchemaChange", change: { kind: "renameCollection", name: string } | { kind: "renameTable", tableId: UUID, name: string } | { kind: "renameField", tableId: UUID, fieldId: UUID, name: string } | { kind: "changeField", tableId: UUID, fieldId: UUID, type: "text" | "number" | "checkbox" | "date" | "select" | "multi-select" | "url" | "attachment" | "relation", required: boolean } | { kind: "addButton", tableId: UUID, name: string } | { kind: "addField", tableId: UUID, field: { name: string, type: "text" | "number" | "checkbox" | "date" | "select" | "multi-select" | "url" | "attachment", required: boolean, unique: boolean, default?: any JSON, options?: string[] } } } | { workspaceId?: string, datasetPath: string, expectedDatasetId?: UUID, action: "prepareMigration", migrationPath?: string | null } | { workspaceId?: string, action: "migrationPreviewPage", preparationId: UUID, after?: string, limit?: integer } | { workspaceId?: string, action: "approveMigration", agentLabel?: string, preparationId: UUID, revisionSha256: SHA-256 hex, approvalDigest: SHA-256 hex, changeSha256?: SHA-256 hex } | { workspaceId?: string, action: "discardMigration", preparationId: UUID }`. Required.

Returns what that verb returns, listed under [`dohc dataset`](#dohc-dataset). The relay accepts it from an Admin alone.

### `dohc_list_member_apps`

List the apps you can open in this workspace: official apps its owner published (kind workspace), then apps members shared (kind member). Continue with nextCursor until it is null; a page can be empty and still have a next page. url opens the app in a browser. consent says whether the person you work for allowed a Member app: none, current, or changed (allowed an earlier version). Only that person can allow a Member app, in their browser. membersCanShare, on the first page, says whether members may share apps.

- `cursor`: `string`

Returns `{ apps: { kind, publicationId, name, authorName, createdAtMs, reachable, consent, canWithdraw, url }[], nextCursor, membersCanShare? }`.

### `dohc_inspect_member_app`

Show what a Member app can do before anyone allows it: its author, each Collection with the access and actions it uses (readOnly false changes data), and its source files. dohc_read_member_app_source reads one file. dohc_fork_member_app copies the source into a Personal app.

- `publicationId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ name, authorName, consent, collections: { name, access, operations }[], source: { path, sha256, byteLength }[] }`.

### `dohc_read_member_app_source`

Read one source file of a Member app, by a path dohc_inspect_member_app lists. text is null when the file is not UTF-8 text or is larger than 256 KiB; byteLength is its size.

- `publicationId`: `string`. Required.
- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ path, byteLength, text }`.

### `dohc_share_member_app`

Share a Personal app (a folder in the Personal app folder) with the members of a workspace you joined, or update the one you shared under the same slug. Members review and allow it in their browser before it runs. It can do only what both its author and each viewer can do.

- `personalApp`: `string`. Required.
- `slug`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, publicationId, slug } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_fork_member_app`

Copy a Member app's source into a new folder in the Personal app folder, to read or change it. The copy is a Personal app that only you use until you approve or share it. Refuses a folder that exists.

- `publicationId`: `string`. Required.
- `personalApp`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, personalApp } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_promote_member_app`

Copy a Member app's source into a new folder of a synced workspace the person you work for owns, on Main, so its owner can review and publish it as an official app. Refuses a folder that exists and apps that call outside services. The copy runs for no one until the owner publishes it. Ask the person you work for first.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `publicationId`: `string`. Required.
- `folder`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, folder } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_withdraw_member_app`

Stop sharing a Member app. Authors withdraw their own; the workspace owner and admins can withdraw any member's app. Members can no longer open it. The author can share it again. Ask the person you work for before you withdraw someone else's app.

- `publicationId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, publicationId } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_set_member_app_sharing`

Turn on or off whether members of a workspace can share apps with each other. Only its owner and admins can change it. Off pauses the apps members shared until it is on again; apps admins shared keep working. Ask the person you work for first.

- `membersCanShare`: `boolean`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, membersCanShare } | { ok: false, reason }`.

---

**Internal sync, live-document, and recovery.** Operational tools for pausing sync, managing live-editing sessions, held changes, outside edits, and retained/kept copies. Ordinary building rarely needs these.

### `dohc_stop_workspace_sync`

Stop this computer's sync for the owning workspace after saving live document edits. Keep local work, shares, history, and protected-file keys. Groups you joined and received-share mounts keep syncing. Record who paused and when. Resume in Settings.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

No arguments.

Returns `{ ok: true, workspaceId, workspaceSynced: false, syncPause?: { atMs, author } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_live_documents`

List this workspace's live documents, as Live documents shows them in dohc. Each row has `path`, `objectId`, `status` (`ready`, `preparing`, `paused`, `unavailable`, or `retired` once live editing stopped), `reason` when it is not live, and `canResume`, true when dohc_resume_live_editing can start it again. `document-unavailable`: The file moved or was removed on this computer. Review it in Live documents. `workspace-changed`: The workspace changed while live editing ran. Review it in Live documents. `session-host-refused`: The server stopped live editing. The file and its history are unchanged. Resume tries again. `session-host-diverged`: The server's copy no longer matches the synced one. Resume and Stop can't help. Contact the server's operator. `live-document-without-lineage`: Live editing can't start until the document is opened once in dohc. Open it, then Resume. `live-document-too-large`: The note is larger than 256 KB, so it can't be edited live, and Resume can't start it. Make it smaller or split it, then open it in dohc and Resume. `live-edit-unadmitted`: The server hasn't applied an edit. Resume tries again. `conflict-parent-withheld`: A conflict in the file was resolved, so live editing can't resume. Edits made in dohc may not reach people with the link. A copy can go live, but it leaves out the row's kept edits. Save a recovery copy to keep them. Then duplicate the file and open the copy in dohc. If only this file was shared, share the copy too. `live-history-over-budget`: The document's edit history is too long for the server to check, so live editing can't start. Edits still sync, but people it is shared with can't edit it live.
