Resume tries again now. `live-start-failing`: The server can't start live editing and keeps trying. failure.word is the server's reason, and failure.since is when it began. Resume tries now. `note-format-off`: The server turned off the newer note format this document uses. Resume can't help. Contact the server's operator. `failure` `{ word, since }` is the server's word for why a row isn't live and when that began, as on `live-start-failing` rows. `record` is the server's record of the note: `state` (`off`, `starting`, `live`, or `stopping`), `reason` and `cause` for an off note, `generation`, `since`, and `changedBy`. `movedTo` is the path a note moved to; once stopped, pass `movedTo` to dohc_resume_live_editing to resume directly at that path. `deferredStop` `{ unsentEdits, editable }` is a Stop that waits for unsent edits. `quarantine` is the `recovery` of edits the server refused, with `storedOn` and `incident` as in `keptEdits`; `stopping` means a Stop waits for the server. Pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` until it is null. Owner workspace only.

Live editing belongs to the owner's sharing. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

- `cursor`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, documents: { path, objectId, status, reason?, failure?, canResume, record?, movedTo?, stopped?, deferredStop?, quarantine?, earlier?: true, saveOnly?: true, sessionEnded?: true, storedOn?, incident? }[], nextCursor } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_stop_live_editing`

Stop live editing for a document, as Stop does in Live documents. dohc_resume_live_editing starts it again. dohc records the Stop as this agent's when the server says this request stopped it; `already: true` means live editing was already stopped, and dohc records no one. Pass the row's `objectId` from dohc_list_live_documents to stop the server's document when its file moved or is gone; dohc then stops that document, whatever path it has now. `keptEdits` is `recovered` when dohc wrote edits the server refused into the file, `kept` while dohc still keeps them (see `keptEdits` in dohc_workspace_status), and `none` when there were none. Unlike Stop in Live documents, dohc refuses while the document is open in an editor, where someone may be typing; ask the person using dohc to close it. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `objectId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, keptEdits, already?: true } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_resume_live_editing`

Resume live editing for a document, as Resume does in Live documents. Accepts a row whose `canResume` is true in dohc_list_live_documents. dohc sends this computer's unsent changes first, and records the Resume as this agent's when the server says this request resumed it; `already: true` means it was already live, and dohc records no one. `ended: true` means its file was moved, deleted or replaced: the server's pause of it ended and live editing stays off. Then read dohc_list_live_documents: `preparing` until the server starts the document, then `ready`. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, already?: true, ended?: true } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_held_change`

Read a change dohc held for a Markdown file because saving it would rewrite parts dohc can't show. `file` is the file's text on disk, or null; `held` is what saving the change would write. `change` is null when nothing is held. A change too large to return reports `tooLarge`. When dohc can't preview the change exactly, such as while edits wait to sync, it reports `unavailable` instead.

A shared view holds no saves of its own, so it does not offer this tool.

- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, change: { path, file, held } | { path, tooLarge: true } | { path, unavailable } | null } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_held_note_change`

Review, drop, or undo a held note change. Only a local agent in the owner's workspace may use this. Review names the authors and returns a token. Drop requires that token, saves the waiting text in History, and returns an Undo token. Undo restores the waiting text as held. Neither action rewrites the file or grants conversion consent. Refusals: held-change-stale: Run review again and use its new token for drop. held-change-missing: Read the note again; there is no held change to drop. held-change-conflict: Resolve the conflict before reviewing and dropping again. held-change-undo-stale: Do not retry undo; recover the waiting text from History. held-change-shared-owner: Drop and undo are unavailable for adopted shared notes; leave the held work intact.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `action`: `"review" | "drop" | "undo"`. Required.
- `token`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, token, authors, held, historyMomentId } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_save_recovery_copy`

Save a live document's kept edits next to the document. Kept edits are edits the server refused, which dohc keeps on this computer, or on the server for a document it hosts (`storedOn`); dohc_workspace_status lists them as `keptEdits`. dohc writes a readable Markdown copy next to the document when it can read the edits as a document; `copyPath` is null when it cannot. Kept edits the note has no place for, such as text typed into a part someone else deleted, are listed at the end of the copy, and `notInNote` counts them. dohc also keeps a recovery package with every kept edit on this computer, at `packagePath` in .dohc/local/live-recovery, which does not sync. dohc writes these files itself, not as the agent that asked. For edits the server keeps, dohc then tells the server the copy is saved, and the `recovery` becomes `copied`. `keptEdits` is `kept` when the edits stay where `storedOn` says, `copied` when the server may now release them, and `ended` for edits a Stop could not write: dohc no longer keeps those, and the copy holds them, or the package when `copyPath` is null. Accepts every `recovery`. Pass the `incident` from `keptEdits` to save exactly those kept edits; without it, dohc saves edits a Stop could not write first. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `incident`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, copyPath, packagePath, notInNote, folder, storedOn, keptEdits } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_retry_kept_edits`

Send a live document's kept edits to the server once more, as Try again does in dohc. Take `path` and `incident` from `keptEdits` in dohc_workspace_status. Accepts a `recovery` of `paused`, or `copied` for edits the server keeps. When saveOnly is true, save a recovery copy instead. If recovery is unreadable, retry reads the edits again. Then read dohc_workspace_status: `retrying` until the server answers, `paused` with a new `incident` if it refuses again. A `not-written` or `stopping` document needs dohc_stop_again instead. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `incident`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_stop_again`

Stop live editing again for a document whose Stop kept its edits, as Try again does on its row in dohc. Take `path` and `incident` from `keptEdits` in dohc_workspace_status. Accepts a `recovery` of `not-written`, where dohc writes the kept edits into the file, or `stopping`, where it asks the server again to stop live editing. `keptEdits` is `recovered` once the file holds the edits, `kept` while dohc still keeps them, and `none` when it kept none. dohc refuses while the document is open in an editor. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `incident`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, keptEdits } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_outside_changes`

List live notes whose file changed outside dohc while the note was live. Neither the note nor History holds those changes. Keep one with dohc_keep_outside_change, which saves the file's bytes as a copy and puts the note's text back in the file.

The owning workspace holds outside changes. Shared profiles do not offer this read.

No arguments.

Returns `{ outsideChanges: { path, firstObservedAtMs }[] }`.

### `dohc_keep_outside_change`

Keep a live note's outside change, as Keep a copy does in dohc. Take `path` from dohc_list_outside_changes. dohc saves the file's bytes beside it as a copy, then writes the note's last saved text back into the file. `kept` is false when the file no longer holds an outside change. Owner workspace only.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, kept } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_kept_copies`

List retained copies with a known workspace path, including copies adopted from staging during startup. Each entry names the file (`path`) that has a second copy, hidden until dohc_save_kept_copy moves it beside the file. `more` is true when the workspace kept more than this list holds.

Known copies deleted during replacement do not appear. Adopted staging files without an original path remain in `.dohc/engine/displaced`. Notices offers a recovery-folder action for these files; `watcher.status.keptFiles` also lists them. Copies kept from outside writes are ordinary workspace files listed separately in `outsideWriteCopies` in this tool's response as [original path, copy path, copy id] entries. Open the copy by its workspace path. Changes to protected files such as `.env` that a sync replaced or deleted are listed in `protectedCopies` as [path, id, keptAtMs] entries, kept on this computer only; use dohc_restore_protected_copy or dohc_discard_protected_copy.

No arguments.

Returns `{ ok: true, outsideWriteCopies?, protectedCopies?, keptCopies: { id, path, keptAtMs }[], more } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_save_kept_copy`

Move one kept copy from dohc_list_kept_copies to a visible file beside its file, such as `notes (kept copy).md`. The original file does not change. `status` is `saved` with the copy's `path`: read both, keep what you need, and delete the copy when you are done. `gone` means nothing is kept under that id any more. `no-valid-name` means no name beside the file fits dohc's path limits, so the copy stays kept: rename the file or its folder to something shorter and try again.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `id`: `integer`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, status: "saved", path } | { ok: true, status: "gone" } | { ok: true, status: "no-valid-name" } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_restore_protected_copy`

Write one entry from `protectedCopies` in dohc_list_kept_copies back to its protected file. Each entry is [path, id, keptAtMs]: a change to a protected file such as `.env` that a sync replaced or deleted, kept on this computer only. The synced text stays in the file's History, so the restore can be reversed there. `status` is `restored` with the file's `path`.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `id`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, status: "restored", path } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_discard_protected_copy`

Remove one entry from `protectedCopies` in dohc_list_kept_copies for good. The kept change was never in History, so it cannot be brought back. The protected file does not change. `status` is `discarded` with the file's `path`.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `id`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, status: "discarded", path } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_retained_copies`

List old file copies dohc keeps on a drive that cannot tell it whether another program still has one open, such as a macFUSE volume. dohc never deletes these itself. `total` counts them all, with their logical size in `bytes`; deleting them may free less disk space. `copies` lists those dohc_delete_retained_copies can delete now, oldest first, with the `revision` each delete must match. Copies changed in the last 30 seconds, copies whose file waits for review, and copies an unfinished save still needs are not listed. `more` is true when more copies remain past this list.

A shared view keeps no old file copies, so it does not offer this tool.

No arguments.

Returns `{ ok: true, copies: { id, revision }[], more, total: { count, bytes } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_delete_retained_copies`

Permanently delete up to 100 copies listed by dohc_list_retained_copies. They do not go to the trash. dohc cannot check whether another program still has one open: such a program may lose what it writes next. Ask the person to close other programs that use this workspace first, and set acceptLateWriteRisk to true. A copy that changed since it was listed, or whose file waits for review, is skipped and stays. Returns how many copies were `deleted`, `skipped` and `failed`, and the `remaining` count and bytes. List again to delete more.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `copies`: `({ id: integer, revision: integer })[]`. Required.
- `acceptLateWriteRisk`: `true`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, deleted, skipped, failed, remaining: { count, bytes } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

## CLI

```sh
dohc <command> <verb> [arguments] [options]
```

`dohc --help`, `dohc <command> --help`, and `dohc <command> <verb> --help` print the same summaries, flags, and fields as this section. These options work with every verb:

- `--as-agent`: Post and read chat as an agent.
- `--agent-id <id>`: Work as this agent you run, by its id in Settings › Agents. Implies --as-agent.
- `--workspace <id>`: Work in this workspace, by its id, instead of the one this folder is in. Relative paths then start at the workspace's folder.
- `--json`: Print the result as JSON.
- `--help`: Show help. -h does the same.

Two environment variables also change what the CLI does:

- `DOHC_RUN_ID` links the messages that `post` and `reply` write to a local agent run.
- `DOHC_STATE_DIR` names the app's state folder when the CLI cannot find the running app in its default place.

On Windows, dohc starts a chat agent with `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1`, so in cmd the agent must run a program in the workspace folder as `.\name`, not by its bare name.

### `dohc links`

Read and resolve document links.

`indexBuilding` is true while the link index is being built: seed work, pending updates, or eligible files without an index row. It carries across cursor pages; start a fresh walk to observe completion. `unchecked` names sources that could not be checked, including oversized files. These can keep `complete` false after building stops. `complete` describes the local index; `mountsCovered` separately reports mounted-share coverage. IPC, CLI, and MCP return these same fields.

#### `dohc links edges`

```sh
dohc links edges [options]
```

Read a bounded page of file links.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous page.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, versionId, files: { objectId, path, title }[], entries: { kind, source, target, ordinal }[], unchecked, complete, indexBuilding, mountsCovered, nextCursor }`.

#### `dohc links connections`

```sh
dohc links connections [options]
```

Read how Collections, apps, and automations connect.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, scope, nodes: ({ kind: "document-collection", id, title, path, recordCount } | { kind: "dataset", id, title, path, datasetId, firstTableId } | { kind: "app", id, title, path, entryPath } | { kind: "automation", id, title, path, automationId, enabled } | { kind: "group", id, title, channelId })[], edges: { kind, source, target, approval? }[], records: { collection, paths }[], complete, mountsCovered }`.

#### `dohc links in`

```sh
dohc links in <subject-json> [options]
```

Read documents that link to a file.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous page.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, versionId, subject: { path, objectId }, entries: { source, title, ordinal, span, line, highlightStart, highlightEnd, snippet }[], unchecked, complete, indexBuilding, mountsCovered, nextCursor }` or `null`.

#### `dohc links resolve`

```sh
dohc links resolve <source> <literals-json> [options]
```

Resolve links from one document.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, versionId, results: ({ path, fragment } | { path, create, fragment } | null)[], mountsCovered }`.

### `dohc drawing`

Read, create, and edit .excalidraw drawings.

#### `dohc drawing create`

```sh
dohc drawing create <path> [elements-json] [options]
```

Create a drawing, optionally with elements.

Each element is { type: rectangle|ellipse|diamond|text|arrow|line|frame, x, y } with optional id, width, height, text, strokeColor, backgroundColor, points, link, groupIds, and frameId. A text element with containerId sits inside that shape or arrow. An arrow takes start and end element ids to bind its ends. Undo Run in History skips a drawing an agent created, because removing a drawing can also remove linked assets: delete it individually from History. It also skips a drawing open in an editor until it closes.

- `--request-id <id>`: Create it at most once for this id.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, elements: { id, version }[], warning? }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc drawing edit`

```sh
dohc drawing edit <path> <edit-json> [options]
```

Add, change, or delete a drawing's elements.

edit-json is { add, update, delete }. update and delete name each element's id and the expectedVersion drawing read gave; dohc refuses the whole edit when someone changed that element since. Each element is { type: rectangle|ellipse|diamond|text|arrow|line|frame, x, y } with optional id, width, height, text, strokeColor, backgroundColor, points, link, groupIds, and frameId. A text element with containerId sits inside that shape or arrow. An arrow takes start and end element ids to bind its ends. Undo Run in History skips a drawing an agent created, because removing a drawing can also remove linked assets: delete it individually from History. It also skips a drawing open in an editor until it closes.

- `--request-id <id>`: Apply it at most once for this id.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, elements: { id, version }[], warning? }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc drawing read`

```sh
dohc drawing read <path> [options]
```

Read a drawing's elements, as an open canvas holds them.

- `--points`: Include line, arrow, and freehand points.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, path, live, elements: { id, type, version, x, y, width, height, angle?, text?, strokeColor?, backgroundColor?, link?, groupIds?, frameId?, containerId?, startBinding?, endBinding?, boundElements?, points?, pointCount? }[], appState }`.

### `dohc notices`

Read this workspace's Notices.

Listing does not change whether rows are read.

#### `dohc notices list`

```sh
dohc notices list [options]
```

List this workspace's Notices, newest first: each row's title, text, sender, time, whether you have read it, and where it opens.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, notices: { kind, id, title, body, sender, createdAtMs, read, opens, note? }[] }`.

### `dohc inbox`

Capture notes and links into the workspace Inbox and triage them.

Creates Inbox/ lazily on first capture. Listing does not create Inbox/.

#### `dohc inbox add`

```sh
dohc inbox add [body] [options]
```

Capture a note or link into the workspace Inbox.

Creates Inbox/ lazily on first capture.

- `--title <<text>>`: Title for the Inbox item.
- `--url <<https://...>>`: Optional http or https link to capture.
- `--kind <<note|file|image|link|webhook>>`: Item kind (defaults to link when --url is set, otherwise note).

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, recordId, title, createdInbox }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc inbox archive`

```sh
dohc inbox archive <path> [options]
```

Mark an Inbox item as Archived.

Updates Status to Archived through the item's live document session.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, previousStatus, changed }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc inbox move`

```sh
dohc inbox move <path> <folder> [options]
```

Move an Inbox item (and any linked Inbox attachments) into an owned folder.

Rewrites workspace links and returns History operation id(s) for Undo. Use "" or "." as <folder> to move into the workspace root.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, fromPath, toPath, operationId?, attachments: { fromPath, toPath, operationId? }[] }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc inbox list`

```sh
dohc inbox list [options]
```

List items waiting in the workspace Inbox.

- `--status <<New|Filed|Archived>>`: Filter items by status.
- `--limit <<n>>`: Show at most this many items (default 50, max 100).

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, exists, items: { kind, id, path, title, status, source, received, url?, attachment?, filedTo? }[], hasMore }`.

### `dohc webhook`

List and create incoming webhooks that add records to Collections.

Only the owner's own agents can use them, in a synced workspace.

#### `dohc webhook list`

```sh
dohc webhook list [options]
```

List this workspace's incoming webhooks and their recent deliveries.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, kind: "none" }` or `{ schemaVersion, kind: "unavailable", message }` or `{ schemaVersion, kind: "ready", serverOrigin, webhooks: { webhookId, name, collectionPath, collectionId, paused, pauseReason, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, lastDeliveryAtMs, pendingCount, recentDeliveries }[], limit }`.

#### `dohc webhook create`

```sh
dohc webhook create <name> [options]
```

Create an incoming webhook address that adds records to a private Collection.

The address is a secret: anyone who has it can add records. dohc shows it once. If you don't know whether a create worked, run dohc webhook list before you try again. Creating needs the server to run this workspace's automations, with no handover waiting, and a synced Collection.

- `--collection <path>`: Required. The Collection's folder, relative to the workspace root.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, webhook: { webhookId, name, collectionPath, collectionId, paused, pauseReason, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, lastDeliveryAtMs, pendingCount, recentDeliveries }, endpointUrl }`.

### `dohc member-apps`

List the apps you can open in this workspace, review Member apps, and share or copy your Personal apps.

Members allow a Member app in their browser. Agents can list, review, share, and copy apps, but never allow one.

#### `dohc member-apps share`

```sh
dohc member-apps share <app-folder> [options]
```

Share a Personal app with the workspace's members, or update it.

Sharing again under the same name updates the app. Members allow it again.

- `--slug <<name>>`: Name the app keeps in the workspace (default: the folder name).

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, publicationId, slug }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc member-apps fork`

```sh
dohc member-apps fork <app-id> <new-folder> [options]
```

Copy a Member app's source into a new Personal app folder.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, personalApp }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc member-apps promote`

```sh
dohc member-apps promote <app-id> <new-folder> [options]
```

Copy a Member app's source into a new folder of the workspace you own.

Only the owner can promote, on Main of a synced workspace. Publish the copy with Review app, which shows what it can reach.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, folder }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc member-apps withdraw`

```sh
dohc member-apps withdraw <app-id> [options]
```

Stop sharing a Member app with the workspace.

Authors withdraw their own apps. The owner and admins can withdraw any. Sharing it again brings it back.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, publicationId }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc member-apps sharing`

```sh
dohc member-apps sharing <on|off> [options]
```

Turn members' app sharing on or off.

Only the owner and admins can change it. Off pauses the apps members shared until it is on again. Apps admins shared keep working.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, membersCanShare }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc member-apps list`

```sh
dohc member-apps list [options]
```

List the workspace's official apps, then the apps members shared.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous page.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, apps: { kind, publicationId, name, authorName, createdAtMs, reachable, consent, canWithdraw, url }[], nextCursor, membersCanShare? }`.

#### `dohc member-apps inspect`

```sh
dohc member-apps inspect <app-id> [options]
```

Show a Member app's author, Collection access, and source files.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, name, authorName, consent, collections: { name, access, operations }[], source: { path, sha256, byteLength }[] }`.

#### `dohc member-apps source`

```sh
dohc member-apps source <app-id> <path> [options]
```

Print one source file of a Member app.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, path, byteLength, text }`.

### `dohc sync`

Stop syncing this workspace on this computer.

Local files, documents, records, and history stay here. Shares and protected-file keys are retained. Groups you joined and received-share mounts keep syncing. Turn sync on in Settings to resume the same workspace.

The pause result records who paused and when. A person author has kind person, personId, and self. Show you when self is true. Person pause labels do not use profile names. An agent author has kind agent, agentId, onBehalfOf, and depth. Agent names are provenance and grant no authority.

#### `dohc sync stop`

```sh
dohc sync stop [options]
```

Stop this computer's sync after saving live document edits.

- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name when --as-agent is set.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, workspaceId, workspaceSynced: false, syncPause?: { atMs, author } }`.

### `dohc access`

Read observed grants and request fresh Sharing inventories.

Answers describe observed grants, not authorization. An empty page means no matching grants within its coverage. Paths resolve from your current folder. Received selectors use their source workspace's coordinates.

The object and sharing verbs return only the allowlisted AccessAnswer fields shown below, with at most 100 rows per page. They never return credentials, bearer URLs, invitation URLs, share codes, or link URLs.

Share queries use the current observation. Use `dohc access refresh` to request fresh Sharing inventories through the same paced owner as opening Sharing. Its `status` is `requested`, `joined`, `paced`, or `unavailable`. Unavailable answers include `reason`: `signed-out` or `unreadable`. Requested and joined wait for started or existing attempts to settle, without promising success. Within a minute of the workspace's last check, it waits for the next one. Paced means only shares with you follow the existing refresh schedule. Read `dohc access sharing` afterward to inspect observations. `freshness` is `fresh`, `stale`, or `unknown`; `checkedAtMs` is the observation timestamp in milliseconds, or null when unknown. `coverage` names the observed scope and whether it is complete. Its `observation` is `interval`: pages do not form an atomic snapshot. `nextCursor` continues the answer, or is null at the end.

`unknownReason` is null when coverage is known. When visibility is `hidden` or `missing`, it is null because visibility states why the answer is unavailable. Every other answer with `coverage.kind` set to `unavailable` requires one reason. Its closed values are `signed-out`, `not-synced`, `other-account`, `other-server`, `not-listed-yet`, `changed`, and `unreadable`. Reasons describe only this device's records and account. They contain no account identity, email, server URL, share id, or path.

Queries use only the CLI's registered workspace, with no workspace enumeration. The granted lane contains that workspace owner's grants; the received lane contains the signed-in account's received shares. A received object's answer shows only the recipient's own grant.

Collection answers report current access and capabilities, not share grants.

#### `dohc access refresh`

```sh
dohc access refresh [options]
```

Request fresh Sharing observations with the same pacing as opening Sharing.

Reports requested, joined, paced, or unavailable. Requested and joined wait for started or existing attempts to settle, without promising success. Within a minute of the workspace's last check, it waits for the next one. Paced means only shares with you follow the existing refresh schedule. Read access sharing afterward to inspect observations.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "unavailable", reason }`. Uses socket verb `accessRefresh`.

#### `dohc access object`

```sh
dohc access object <reference-json> [options]
```

Read the grants covering an object.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous answer.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ref: { kind: "path", path, versionId } | { kind: "file", objectId } | { kind: "chat", channelWireId } | { kind: "collection", datasetId } | null, rows: ({ kind: "share", shareId, grantId, via, granterUserId, granterEmail, recipientUserId, recipientEmail, subjectName, sharerName, selector, access, status, generation, fileScope?, removalMessage? } | { kind: "collection", datasetId, principal, appId, operationIds, revision, revisionSha256, compatible })[], visibility, coverage: { kind, complete, observation: "interval" }, unknownReason, checkedAtMs, freshness, nextCursor }`. Uses socket verb `accessObject`.

#### `dohc access sharing`

```sh
dohc access sharing <granted|received> [options]
```

Page this workspace's granted shares or this account's received shares.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous answer.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ref: { kind: "path", path, versionId } | { kind: "file", objectId } | { kind: "chat", channelWireId } | { kind: "collection", datasetId } | null, rows: ({ kind: "share", shareId, grantId, via, granterUserId, granterEmail, recipientUserId, recipientEmail, subjectName, sharerName, selector, access, status, generation, fileScope?, removalMessage? } | { kind: "collection", datasetId, principal, appId, operationIds, revision, revisionSha256, compatible })[], visibility, coverage: { kind, complete, observation: "interval" }, unknownReason, checkedAtMs, freshness, nextCursor }`. Uses socket verb `accessSharing`.

### `dohc share`

Read copy details, and list and disconnect a link's agents.

Requires the original workspace and its signed-in owner account.

#### `dohc share copy`

```sh
dohc share copy <shareId> <grantId> [options]
```

Read a grant's share code and named-account invite link.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "active", shareCode, browserInvitationUrl? }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "ended" }`.

#### `dohc share agents`

```sh
dohc share agents <shareId> <grantId> [options]
```

List the agents connected through a share link.

Find a link's share id and grant id with dohc access sharing granted. Each name is the one the agent reported. dohc cannot check it.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous page.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, agents: { connectionId, reportedName, connectedAtMs, lastActionAtMs }[], nextCursor }`.

#### `dohc share disconnect`

```sh
dohc share disconnect <shareId> <grantId> <connectionId> [options]
```

Disconnect one agent from a share link.

Find the connection id with dohc share agents.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, connectionId }`.

### `dohc members`

List, invite, and remove the workspace's members, set what they can do, and manage the invite link.

Works in a workspace you own or joined, signed in with the account that owns or joined it. Your server decides what your role allows. Members see names and roles. Admins also invite people, remove members, let them back in, set the member level and a Group's access, and manage the invite link. Only the owner changes roles or ends membership. A person is a member id from dohc members list, or the email of an invite or a person.

#### `dohc members list`

```sh
dohc members list [options]
```

List people, invites, removed accounts, the member level, and the invite link.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members invite`

```sh
dohc members invite <email> [options]
```

Invite someone by email. dohc emails them an invitation when the server sends email, and inviting the same address again emails it again. They join when they sign in to dohc with that address.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members remove`

```sh
dohc members remove <person> [options]
```

Remove a person or cancel an invite. Copies already on their computer stay.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members level`

```sh
dohc members level <view|comment|edit> [options]
```

Set what every member can do: view, comment, or edit. Admins and the owner always edit.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members admin`

```sh
dohc members admin <person> [options]
```

Make a member an admin. Admins invite, remove members, and manage the invite link.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members member`

```sh
dohc members member <person> [options]
```

Make an admin a member again.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members let-back-in`

```sh
dohc members let-back-in <person> [options]
```

Let a removed account back in as a member.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members link`

```sh
dohc members link <on|off|reset> [options]
```

Turn the invite link on or off, or reset it.

Anyone with the link who signs in becomes a member. Turning it off or resetting it removes no one who already joined. Reset stops the old link working. dohc members list shows the link.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members group`

```sh
dohc members group <group> [options]
```

Show or set what members can do in a Group: post, view, or none. Admins and the owner always post.

A Group is a name or id from dohc chat groups. General, direct messages and agents' chats have no access of their own. With none, members no longer see the Group. People who read it may keep a copy.

- `--level <post|view|none>`: Set the Group's access.
- `--clear`: Remove the Group's access, so it takes the member level.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members folder`

```sh
dohc members folder <path> [options]
```

Set or clear access to a workspace folder.

Use a workspace-relative path, or / for the workspace root. Each run sets the whole rule. Repeat --person for everyone the rule keeps. Copies already on people's computers stay when access narrows.

- `--members <view|comment|edit|none>`: Set the member level.
- `--person <email=level>`: Set one person's level. Repeat for more people.
- `--clear`: Remove the folder's rule.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members remove-folder-marker`

```sh
dohc members remove-folder-marker <path> [options]
```

Remove an unknown or unreadable folder marker.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

#### `dohc members end`

```sh
dohc members end [options]
```

End membership for everyone. Members lose access; copies already on their computers stay.

- `--everyone`: Required. Confirms that every member and admin loses access.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, status: "ready", view: { workspaceId, workspaceName, viewer, memberLevel, inviteLink, groupRules, folderRules, people }, invitation?: { invitationEmail } | { invitationEmail: "limit", invitationEmailLimit } }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "refused" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "done" }` or `{ schemaVersion, status: "group", name, level, memberLevel }`.

### `dohc document`

Read, edit, and create live Markdown documents. List and start chats on tracked files. List, stop, and resume live documents, and recover edits the server refused.

Paths resolve from your current folder. Changes are recorded as an agent's, as with MCP. A refusal exits with status 1 and prints its reason to stderr, including with --json.

#### `dohc document read`

```sh
dohc document read <path> [options]
```

Read the current Markdown, including edits in an open editor.

Read before editing. Without --json, prints the Markdown byte for byte.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, markdown }`.

#### `dohc document held`

```sh
dohc document held <path> [options]
```

Show a change dohc held: the file's text and what saving the change would write.

Prints null when nothing is held for the file.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, change: { path, file, held } | { path, tooLarge: true } | { path, unavailable } | null }`.

#### `dohc document held-change`

```sh
dohc document held-change <path> [options]
```

Review, drop, or undo a held change on the owner's computer.

held-change-stale: Run review again and use its new token for drop. held-change-missing: Read the note again; there is no held change to drop. held-change-conflict: Resolve the conflict before reviewing and dropping again. held-change-undo-stale: Do not retry undo; recover the waiting text from History. held-change-shared-owner: Drop and undo are unavailable for adopted shared notes; leave the held work intact.

- `--action <review|drop|undo>`: Review returns the token needed for Drop.
- `--token <token>`: Use the review token for Drop or the Drop token for Undo.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, token, authors, held, historyMomentId }`.

#### `dohc document edit`

```sh
dohc document edit <path> [-] [options]
```

Replace matching text or append Markdown through the live document.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. Use --text instead to supply the body as an argument. Each side allows at most 256 KiB of UTF-8. Edits change the body, not frontmatter. Concurrent editing can prevent removing blocks or changing their kind. A pending warning means the edit is saved locally and the shared file update is pending. Do not repeat it. Read again after other warnings or an unexplained failure. Retry keys have the same limits as dohc_edit_document.

- `--text <markdown>`: Use this Markdown as the body. An empty string is allowed.
- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name with the change.
- `--find <markdown>`: Replace this exact, unique match. Omit to append.
- `--request-id <key>`: Reuse this key when retrying the same edit, as with dohc_edit_document.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, changed, warning? }`.

#### `dohc document create`

```sh
dohc document create <path> [-] [options]
```

Create a Markdown document without overwriting an existing file.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. Use --text instead to supply Markdown. With neither, create an empty document. The path must end in .md or .markdown. Frontmatter is refused.

- `--text <markdown>`: Use this Markdown as the body. An empty string is allowed.
- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name with the change.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path }`.

#### `dohc document set-fields`

```sh
dohc document set-fields <record> [options]
```

Set fields on a Collection record.

The change lands in the record's frontmatter, and record history attributes it to the agent.

- `--field <name=value>`: Set this field to this text. Repeat for more fields.
- `--fields-json <json>`: Set fields from a JSON object, such as {"points":3,"done":true,"tags":["a"],"due":null}.
- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name with the change.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, recordPath }`.

#### `dohc document chats`

```sh
dohc document chats <path> [options]
```

List chats linked to a workspace file.

Chats follow the file across renames. Use chat show --peek with a thread ID to read it without marking it read.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, fileObjectId, threads: { id, title, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, linkedPathHint? }[] }`.

#### `dohc document comment`

```sh
dohc document comment <path> [-] [options]
```

Start a chat linked to a file with its first message.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. The first message allows at most 64 KiB of UTF-8. Start the first message with a Markdown quote of a passage, as in > the passage, to comment on that passage. The file's editor highlights it.

- `--title <title>`: Set the chat title. Use 1 to 200 characters that are not all whitespace.
- `--text <markdown>`: Set the first message as Markdown. The message must contain text that is not all whitespace.
- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name with the change.
- `--request-id <key>`: Set a key for safe retries. Use 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters. A retry with the same key and the same payload returns the existing result. A retry with the same key and a changed payload is refused.
- `--run-id <id>`: Set the run ID. The value must not be empty. This flag overrides DOHC_RUN_ID.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, threadId, messageId, warning? }`.

#### `dohc document kept-edits`

```sh
dohc document kept-edits [options]
```

List live documents whose edits the server refused or has not accepted yet, and where dohc keeps those edits.

storedOn is this-computer, or server for a document the server hosts. A recovery of paused means the edits wait for you. Save a recovery copy, or try again. A new refusal changes the incident. When saveOnly is true, save a recovery copy instead. If recovery is unreadable, retry reads the edits again. A recovery of not-written or stopping means a Stop kept the edits. Run stop-again to finish it. A recovery of cannot-write means only a recovery copy can return the edits. Copied means a recovery copy of edits the server keeps is saved. If the server accepts a later edit to the document, copied returns to paused. Save another recovery copy to include that edit. A recovery of unreadable means dohc could not read the edits it keeps on this computer, and reason says why. Run retry-kept-edits to read them again. earlier is true when the server keeps the edits in an earlier copy of the workspace. Save a recovery copy to get them back; try again cannot reach them. pendingShare lists shared notes whose edits wait on this computer for the server. Each file holds older text until the server accepts them; document read returns the current text. pendingShareWhileOpen lists new notes shared by a link or with a person, which the server has no file for yet. Each file is current here and reaches the server once its editor in dohc is left. A share made on another computer counts after dohc next lists this workspace's shares.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, keptEdits: { path, reason, storedOn, incident, recovery, earlier?: true, saveOnly?: true }[], pendingShare, pendingShareWhileOpen }`.

#### `dohc document keep-outside-change`

```sh
dohc document keep-outside-change <path> [options]
```

Keep a live note's outside change as a copy and put the note's text back in its file.

Take the path from outside-changes. dohc saves the file's bytes beside it as a copy, then writes the note's last saved text into the file. kept is false when the file no longer holds an outside change.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, kept }`.

#### `dohc document save-recovery-copy`

```sh
dohc document save-recovery-copy <path> [<incident>] [options]
```

Save a document's kept edits next to it.

Accepts every recovery but unreadable. With an incident from kept-edits, dohc saves exactly those kept edits. Without one, it saves edits a Stop could not write first. dohc writes a readable copy next to the document when it can read the edits as a document. Kept edits the note has no place for are listed at the end of the copy, and notInNote counts them. dohc also keeps a recovery package with every kept edit on this computer, in .dohc/local/live-recovery, which does not sync. For edits the server keeps, dohc then tells the server the copy is saved, and the recovery becomes copied. keptEdits is kept when the edits stay where storedOn says, and copied when the server may now release them. It is ended for edits a Stop could not write: dohc no longer keeps them, and the copy holds them, or the package when there is no copy. dohc writes these files itself, not as the agent that asked.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, copyPath, packagePath, notInNote, folder, storedOn, keptEdits }`.

#### `dohc document retry-kept-edits`

```sh
dohc document retry-kept-edits <path> <incident> [options]
```

Send a document's kept edits to the server once more.

Take the incident from kept-edits. Accepts a recovery of paused, or copied for edits the server keeps. For unreadable, dohc reads the kept edits again. It fails with the reason while it still cannot read them. A not-written or stopping document needs stop-again instead. Run kept-edits again to follow it: retrying until the server answers, paused with a new incident if it refuses again.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path }`.

#### `dohc document stop-again`

```sh
dohc document stop-again <path> <incident> [options]
```

Stop live editing again for a document whose Stop kept its edits.

Take the incident from kept-edits. Accepts a recovery of not-written or stopping. For not-written, dohc writes the kept edits into the file. For stopping, it asks the server again to stop live editing. keptEdits is recovered once the file holds the edits, kept while dohc still keeps them, and none when it kept none. dohc refuses while the document is open in an editor. Run kept-edits again to follow it.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, keptEdits }`.

#### `dohc document live`

```sh
dohc document live [options]
```

List this workspace's live documents, with each one's state and why.

status is ready, preparing, paused, unavailable, or retired once live editing stopped. stopped is false on a retired document the server released without its owner's Pause or Stop. reason says why a document is not live. canResume is true when resume can start it again. document-unavailable: The file moved or was removed on this computer. Review it in Live documents. workspace-changed: The workspace changed while live editing ran. Review it in Live documents. session-host-refused: The server stopped live editing. The file and its history are unchanged. Resume tries again. session-host-diverged: The server's copy no longer matches the synced one. Resume and Stop can't help. Contact the server's operator. live-document-without-lineage: Live editing can't start until the document is opened once in dohc. Open it, then Resume. live-document-too-large: The note is larger than 256 KB, so it can't be edited live, and Resume can't start it. Make it smaller or split it, then open it in dohc and Resume. live-edit-unadmitted: The server hasn't applied an edit. Resume tries again. conflict-parent-withheld: A conflict in the file was resolved, so live editing can't resume. Edits made in dohc may not reach people with the link. A copy can go live, but it leaves out the row's kept edits. Save a recovery copy to keep them. Then duplicate the file and open the copy in dohc. If only this file was shared, share the copy too. live-history-over-budget: The document's edit history is too long for the server to check, so live editing can't start. Edits still sync, but people it is shared with can't edit it live. Resume tries again now. live-start-failing: The server can't start live editing and keeps trying. failure.word is the server's reason, and failure.since is when it began. Resume tries now. note-format-off: The server turned off the newer note format this document uses. Resume can't help. Contact the server's operator. deferredStop is a Stop that waits for unsentEdits to reach the server. editable says whether the document still takes edits. quarantine is the recovery of edits the server refused, as kept-edits lists them. stopping means a Stop waits for the server. Pass nextCursor as --cursor until it is null.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous page.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, documents: { path, objectId, status, reason?, failure?, canResume, record?, movedTo?, stopped?, deferredStop?, quarantine?, earlier?: true, saveOnly?: true, sessionEnded?: true, storedOn?, incident? }[], nextCursor }`.

#### `dohc document stop`

```sh
dohc document stop <path> [options]
```

Stop live editing for a document, as Stop does in Live documents.

Run resume to start live editing again. dohc records the Stop as this agent's when the server says this request stopped it. already is true when live editing was already stopped. Then dohc records no one. Pass --object-id from live to stop the server's document when its file moved or is gone. dohc then stops that document, whatever path it has now. keptEdits is recovered when dohc wrote edits the server refused into the file, kept while dohc still keeps them, and none when there were none. For kept, run kept-edits, then save-recovery-copy or stop-again. Unlike Stop in Live documents, dohc refuses while the document is open in an editor, where someone may be typing. Ask the person using dohc to close it.

- `--object-id <id>`: Stop the server's document with this objectId from live.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, keptEdits, already?: true }`.

#### `dohc document resume`

```sh
dohc document resume <path> [options]
```

Resume live editing for a document, as Resume does in Live documents.

Accepts a document whose canResume is true in live. dohc sends this computer's unsent changes first, and records the Resume as this agent's when the server says this request resumed it. already is true when the document was already live. Then dohc records no one. Run live again to follow it: preparing until the server starts the document, then ready.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, already?: true, ended?: true }`.

#### `dohc document outside-changes`

```sh
dohc document outside-changes [options]
```

List live notes whose file changed outside dohc.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, outsideChanges: { path, firstObservedAtMs }[] }`.

### `dohc collection`

Query, read, and create Collection records, and check a collection.yaml file.

Name a Collection by its folder. Paths resolve from your current folder. Changes are recorded as an agent's, as with MCP. Field values are JSON. Set fields on a record with document set-fields.

#### `dohc collection query`

```sh
dohc collection query <collection> [options]
```

List a Collection's records and their field values.

- `--filter <json>`: Keep the records that match, such as {"field":"status","operator":"equals","value":"Open"}. The operator is equals or contains.
- `--sort <field[:desc]>`: Sort by this field, ascending unless it ends in :desc. Repeat to break ties.
- `--group-by <field>`: Group the records by this field.
- `--resolve-relations`: Add the label of each record a relation field names.
- `--limit <count>`: List at most this many records, up to 500.
- `--cursor <json>`: Continue from the nextCursor an earlier query printed.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, collection: { path, status, reasons }, records: { id, path, conflicted, values }[], groups: { value, records }[] | null, nextCursor: { sortValues, recordPath, recordId } | null }`.

#### `dohc collection read-record`

```sh
dohc collection read-record <collection> <record> [options]
```

Read one record of a Collection and the history of its fields.

Name the record by its id, as collection query prints it.

- `--history-limit <count>`: List at most this many field changes, up to 500. The default is 50.
- `--before <history-id>`: List the changes before this historyId from an earlier read.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, collection: { path, status, reasons }, record: { id, path, conflicted, values }, history: { historyId, field, previous, next, authorOriginId, actorKind, onBehalfOf, depth, recordedAtMs, linkAuthor, automationRun }[] }`.

#### `dohc collection create-record`

```sh
dohc collection create-record <collection> <name> [options]
```

Create a record: a new Markdown file in the Collection's folder.

The name is the file name without .md.

- `--field <name=value>`: Set this field to this text. Repeat for more fields.
- `--fields-json <json>`: Set fields from a JSON object, such as {"points":3,"done":true,"tags":["a"],"due":null}.
- `--record-id <id>`: Give the record this id: rec_ and 26 characters from a to z and 2 to 7.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, recordId, recordPath, kept? }`.

#### `dohc collection validate`

```sh
dohc collection validate <path> [options]
```

Check a collection.yaml file and list its problems.

Runs without the dohc app. Exits with status 1 when the file has problems. Each problem names a code and a JSON Pointer into the file.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok, path, diagnostics: { code, path, line?, automation? }[] }`.

### `dohc chat`

Read and post in Groups and threads.

Name a Group by its name or ID, and a thread or message by its ID. A unique ID prefix also works. DOHC_CHAT_ACTOR=agent in the environment does the same as --as-agent.

#### `dohc chat groups`

```sh
dohc chat groups [options]
```

List the Groups in this workspace.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, groups: { kind, id, name, slug, purpose?, channelWireId? }[] }`.

#### `dohc chat link`

```sh
dohc chat link [options]
```

Make a link to put in a chat message.

Give exactly one flag. Put the printed @[work:...] text in a message: it shows as a chip that opens what it names. The link keeps working after a rename or a move. Someone who cannot see what it names sees it as unavailable.

- `--group <group>`: Link a Group, DM, or agent chat, by name, #slug, or id.
- `--thread <id>`: Link a thread.
- `--message <id>`: Link a message.
- `--path <path>`: Link a file, or an app or a Collection by its folder.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, kind, reference, link }`.

#### `dohc chat create-group`

```sh
dohc chat create-group <name> [options]
```

Create a Group and its folder, as New group does.

The folder is the Group's name as a slug. A Group with the same name is refused. A Group made with --level has no folder. Choosing a level needs a connection.

- `--purpose <text>`: Say what the Group is for, in up to 200 characters.
- `--type <posts|chat|both>`: Choose what the Group holds. The default is both.
- `--level <post|view|none>`: Set what members can do in the Group as it is made. With none, members never see it.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, group: { kind, id, name, slug, purpose? } }`.

#### `dohc chat threads`

```sh
dohc chat threads <group> [options]
```

List the threads in a Group.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, group: { kind, id, name, slug, purpose? }, threads: { lane?, id, title, commentCount, openDecisionCount, unread, updatedAtMs }[] }`.

#### `dohc chat watch`

```sh
dohc chat watch [options]
```

Wait for the agent's unread messages. Repeat until interrupted; never mark messages read.

In a run dohc started, watch returns the run's own requests, including replies to its posts. Those messages start no new run.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue from the cursor returned by watch.
- `--group <group>`: Wait only for messages in this Group.
- `--thread <thread>`: Wait only for messages in this thread.
- `--timeout <seconds>`: Wait up to this many seconds per batch. The default and maximum are 25.
- `--once`: Return after one batch, including an empty batch at the timeout.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, messages: { threadId, messageId, group, author, createdAtMs, text }[], cursor }`.

#### `dohc chat inbox`

```sh
dohc chat inbox [options]
```

List unread threads. For an agent, also list its unread requests: mentions of it, its DMs, and replies in threads it posted in.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, threads: { lane?, id, title, commentCount, openDecisionCount, unread, updatedAtMs, group }[], mentions: { threadId, messageId, group, author, createdAtMs, text }[] }`.

#### `dohc chat show`

```sh
dohc chat show <thread-message-or-group> [options]
```

Show a thread or message and mark the thread read, or show a group's posts and conversation.

- `--peek`: Show it without changing what is marked read. A read-only shared view requires it.
- `--before <position>`: For a group, show the page older than this position, as printed after older:.
- `--limit <count>`: For a group, show at most this many items. The default is 50, the most 100.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, thread: { id, title, group, commentCount, openDecisionCount }, dispatch: { paused, lastRun }, messages: { id, author, body, createdAtMs, parentMessageId?, decisionState?, decisionOptions?, decisionOptionDetails?, decisionChosenOption?, attachments, runId?, agentRequests?, authorReported?, work? }[] }` or `{ schemaVersion, stream: { group, items, nextBefore, readPosition } }`.

#### `dohc chat post`

```sh
dohc chat post <group> <body> [options]
```

Start a thread in a Group.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. In a direct message, use reply instead. With --work, the thread shows a Work card: the status and link of its newest report, marked as reported. Reply with --work again to change it, and give --link again to keep the link. Put options first, then --, then text that starts with a dash.

- `--title <title>`: Set the thread's title.
- `--attach <path>`: Attach a workspace file. Repeat for more files.
- `--needs-decision`: Ask readers for a decision.
- `--option <choice>`: Offer a choice. Repeat for more choices. Implies --needs-decision.
- `--work <status>`: Report where your work outside dohc stands: working, waiting, done, failed, stopped. Only an agent reports work.
- `--link <url>`: Link to that work, such as its thread or pull request: an http or https address in plain ASCII. Needs --work.
- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name when --as-agent is set.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, group: { kind, id, name, slug, purpose? }, threadId, messageId, title, warning? }`.

#### `dohc chat reply`

```sh
dohc chat reply <thread> <body> [options]
```

Reply in a thread.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. With --work, the thread shows a Work card: the status and link of its newest report, marked as reported. Reply with --work again to change it, and give --link again to keep the link. Put options first, then --, then text that starts with a dash.

- `--to <message>`: Reply to this message in the thread.
- `--attach <path>`: Attach a workspace file. Repeat for more files.
- `--needs-decision`: Ask readers for a decision.
- `--option <choice>`: Offer a choice. Repeat for more choices. Implies --needs-decision.
- `--resolve <message>`: Resolve this open decision with the reply.
- `--choose <choice>`: Pick this choice of the decision. Needs --resolve.
- `--work <status>`: Report where your work outside dohc stands: working, waiting, done, failed, stopped. Only an agent reports work.
- `--link <url>`: Link to that work, such as its thread or pull request: an http or https address in plain ASCII. Needs --work.
- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name when --as-agent is set.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, threadId, messageId, parentMessageId?, resolvedMessageId?, warning? }`.

#### `dohc chat retry`

```sh
dohc chat retry <thread> [options]
```

Run an agent's stopped request in a conversation again, as Try again does.

dohc chat show reports a stopped run under dispatch.lastRun. Each request gets two attempts. Only the computer that ran it can run it again, and only someone who may post in the conversation.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, status: "queued", threadId }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: false, reason }`.

#### `dohc chat react`

```sh
dohc chat react <message> <emoji> [options]
```

Add your reaction to a message, or remove it if it is already there.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, threadId, messageId, emoji, state }`.

#### `dohc chat delete`

```sh
dohc chat delete <message> [options]
```

Delete a message in a Group or a file's Comments: your own, or any as the owner or an admin.

This can't be undone. The message shows as deleted everywhere it syncs. People who already read it may keep a copy. It needs a workspace that syncs and a connection.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, threadId, messageId, deleted: true }`.

#### `dohc chat grep`

```sh
dohc chat grep <pattern> [options]
```

Search message text and thread titles.

Put options first, then --, then text that starts with a dash.

- `--group <group>`: Search only this Group.
- `--thread <thread>`: Search only this thread.
- `--from <author>`: Match authors: human, agent, or part of a name.
- `--since <when>`: Match messages newer than a date or an age such as 7d.
- `-i`: Ignore case. Without it, a regex or a pattern with capitals matches case.
- `-l`: Print only the IDs of threads that match.
- `-C <count>`: Show this many messages before and after each match.
- `--limit <count>`: Print at most this many results. The default is 100.
- `--regex`: Read the pattern as a regular expression.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, matches: { group, threadId, messageId, author, createdAtMs, text, contextBefore, contextAfter }[] }` or `{ schemaVersion, threadIds }`.

#### `dohc chat export`

```sh
dohc chat export [options]
```

Save threads as Markdown files, one file per thread.

Use at most one of --all, --group, or --thread.

- `--out <folder>`: Write the files to this folder. Required.
- `--all`: Export every thread. This is the default.
- `--group <group>`: Export the threads in one Group.
- `--thread <thread>`: Export one thread.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, files: { threadId, path }[] }`.

#### `dohc chat links`

```sh
dohc chat links <group> [options]
```

Read one page of files mentioned in a chat.

- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous page.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, versionId, subject: { channelWireId }, unchecked, complete, indexBuilding, mountsCovered, sharedChannelRowsUncovered, nextCursor, entries: { threadId, messageId, mentionedAtMs, file, author }[] }` or `null`.

#### `dohc chat file-mentions`

```sh
dohc chat file-mentions [options]
```

Read one bounded page of file mentions.

- `--subject <subject>`: A file path or objectId as JSON.
- `--cursor <cursor>`: Continue the previous page.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, versionId, subject: { objectId, path } | null, entries: { attachment, message, thread, channelId?, channelWireId?, channelName?, channelSlug?, channelKind? }[], unchecked, complete, indexBuilding, mountsCovered, sharedChannelRowsUncovered, nextCursor }` or `null`.

### `dohc dataset`

```sh
dohc dataset <verb> '<JSON>'
```

Create, change, and use transactional Collections.

Each verb takes one JSON object that names workspaceId (or - to read the JSON from stdin, recommended in PowerShell on Windows). Find workspaceId in .dohc/manifest.json at the workspace root. datasetPath is the caller-relative dataset.json path. List and describe return it alongside the internal datasetId. After moving the file, update commands and app manifests. An old path reports a broken reference. These verbs use the same Collection rules as dohc. They never accept caller identity. Only sql accepts SQL, read-only and for the owner.

#### `dohc dataset list`

List Collections.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `after`: `UUID`
- `limit`: `integer`
- `includeArchived`: `boolean`

Returns `{ kind: "list", datasets, nextCursor }` or `{ kind: "collections-refused", refusal: { kind, words } | { kind: "elsewhere", words, computer } }`.

#### `dohc dataset describe`

Show a Collection's tables, fields, and operations.

Use describe to find approved operation IDs.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `includeArchived`: `boolean`

Returns `{ kind: "description", dataset, copy?: { offline, savedAtMs, coverage?: "saved-pages", host?, signedOut?: true, updateFailed?: true } }`.

#### `dohc dataset types`

Write TypeScript types for a Collection's tables and operations.

Writes .dohc/types/<name>.d.ts from the approved revision. Import it with import type. Run it again after a change is approved.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`

Returns `{ kind: "types-written", path, revision }`.

#### `dohc dataset sql`

Run a read-only SQL query or EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN against a Collection.

Owner only. Refuses writes, PRAGMAs, and internal tables. Pass explain: true to inspect SQLite's query plan. Each row lists its values in column order.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `sql`: `string`. Required.
- `params`: `(string | number | null)[]`
- `explain`: `boolean`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "sql", columns, rows, truncated, durationMs, revision, explain, copy?: { offline, savedAtMs, coverage?: "saved-pages", host?, signedOut?: true, updateFailed?: true } }`.

#### `dohc dataset trace`

Show recent operation timings and SQL metrics for a Collection.

Owner only. Keeps the last 200 invocations in memory per Collection.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "trace", entries: { atMs, operation, durationMs, statementCount, rowsRead, changesetBytes, callerKind, revision, status, refusalCode }[], limit }`.

#### `dohc dataset history`

List saved operations, with values to undo edits.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `beforeRevision`: `integer`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "history", datasetId, name?, lineage?, olderRecordedAtMs?, archived?, headRevision, entries: { revision, operation, callerReference, recordedAtMs, approvedRevisionHash, changesetBytes, attachmentCount, undo?, automation?, approvalAgent?, actor?, by?, schema? }[], nextBeforeRevision }`.

#### `dohc dataset historyRevision`

Show the saved source of one past revision.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `revisionSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "history-revision", approvalAgent?: { kind: "agent", label, labelSource: "agent-declared" } | null, revision, schemaSql, operationSource, generatedSources? }`.

#### `dohc dataset prepareHistoryRestore`

Prepare a change that reverses one saved change.

Set `targetRevisionSha256` to `entries[].schema.previousRevisionHash` from `history`. Set `changedRevisionSha256` to `entries[].schema.revisionHash` from `history`. Review the result, then approve it with approveMigration.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `revision`: `integer`. Required.
- `revisionSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `targetRevisionSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `changedRevisionSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "migration-prepared", preparationId, previousRevision, revision, expected: { workspaceId, datasetId, hostEpoch, approvedRevisionHash, revision, digest }, candidate: { candidateId, expected, approvedRevisionHash, checkpointSha256, changeSha256, expiresAtMs, preview }, sourceDigest, approvalDigest, schemaSql, operationSource, migrationSql, expiresAtMs, boundApps?: { scope, publicationId, authorityRevision, appRoot, alias?, shareId?, grantId?, pinnedRevision, pinnedRevisionSha256, operationIds, status, reasons? }[], boundAppsIncomplete?: true }`.

#### `dohc dataset permissions`

List app bindings and explicit data grants.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `after`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "permissions", defaults?: { view, comment, edit, revision, revisionSha256, generation } | null, rules?: { revision, revisionSha256, actions }, permissions: ({ kind: "data", principal, current, metadata } | { kind: "app", principal, current, metadata })[], nextCursor, place?: { kind: "here" } | { kind: "server", host }, boundApps?: { scope, publicationId, authorityRevision, appRoot, alias?, shareId?, grantId?, pinnedRevision, pinnedRevisionSha256, operationIds, status, reasons? }[], boundAppsIncomplete?: true }`.

#### `dohc dataset setGrant`

Add or change an explicit data grant.

grant names revision, revisionSha256, operationIds, and discover.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `grantId`: `string`. Required.
- `grant`: `{ revision: integer, revisionSha256: SHA-256 hex, operationIds: UUID[], discover: boolean }`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "grant-updated" }`.

#### `dohc dataset setDefaults`

Set the actions each workspace level gets in a Collection by default.

defaults names view, comment, and edit operationIds, with revision and revisionSha256. Read them from permissions rules. An Admin runs list, describe, invoke, permissions, setGrant, removeGrant, and setDefaults in a workspace they joined. invoke runs reads, and a write needs a grant that holds it. View and Comment get only reads. No level gets an owner-only action.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `defaults`: `{ view: UUID[], comment: UUID[], edit: UUID[], revision: integer, revisionSha256: SHA-256 hex }`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "grant-updated" }`.

#### `dohc dataset removeGrant`

Remove an explicit data grant.

Set `principalKey` to `permissions[].principal` from `permissions`.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `principalKey`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "grant-updated" }`.

#### `dohc dataset lifecycle`

Show a Collection's archive state and its apps.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `after`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "lifecycle", archived, generation, reason, apps: { appId, binding }[], nextCursor }`.

#### `dohc dataset archive`

Stop a Collection's operations and keep its records.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`

Returns `{ kind: "lifecycle-updated", archived, generation, reason? }`.

#### `dohc dataset restore`

Restore an archived Collection under its rules.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`

Returns `{ kind: "lifecycle-updated", archived, generation, reason? }`.

#### `dohc dataset deletePreview`

Review what deleting a Collection affects.

The result lists affected apps and holds what delete needs.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `after`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "delete-preview", archived, generation, reason, apps: { appId, binding }[], nextCursor, cursor: { workspaceId, datasetId, hostEpoch, approvedRevisionHash, revision, digest }, reviewToken, name, irreversible: true }`.

#### `dohc dataset delete`

Permanently delete a Collection and all its data.

Set `expected` to `cursor` from `deletePreview`. Set `reviewToken` to `reviewToken` from `deletePreview`. Archive the Collection first with dohc dataset archive. Then run deletePreview, since archiving makes an earlier preview stale. This removes the Collection's private data and history. Set acknowledge to true. Export before deleting if you need a recovery copy. Deleted Collections cannot be restored in place.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `expected`: `{ workspaceId: string, datasetId: UUID, hostEpoch: string, approvedRevisionHash: SHA-256 hex, revision: integer, digest: SHA-256 hex }`. Required.
- `reviewToken`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `acknowledge`: `true`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "deleted", deleted: true, datasetId }`.

#### `dohc dataset pendingAttempts`

List pending responses that still hold a retry.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `after`: `integer`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "pending-attempts", datasetId, entries: { reference, operation, recordedAtMs, revision, outcome, attachmentCount }[], nextAfter }`.

#### `dohc dataset reconcileAttempt`

Clear the retry of a saved pending response.

Set `reference` to `entries[].reference` from `pendingAttempts`. Set acknowledge to true. This cannot be undone.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `reference`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `acknowledge`: `true`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "attempt-reconciled", cleared: true }`.

#### `dohc dataset cancelAttempt`

Cancel an unconfirmed pending response.

Set `reference` to `entries[].reference` from `pendingAttempts`. Set acknowledge to true.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `reference`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `acknowledge`: `true`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "attempt-cancelled", cancelled: true }`.

#### `dohc dataset cancelInvoke`

Request cancellation of a running Collection action.

Use the invocationId sent with invoke. The action may already have changed records. Check records or History. Retry with the same input and idempotencyKey.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `invocationId`: `UUID`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "invoke-cancel-requested", outcome: "unknown" }`.

#### `dohc dataset export`

Save a private recovery archive of a Collection.

savePath is an absolute path outside the workspace ending in .dohc-recovery. Set overwrite to true to replace a file. Recovery archives contain private records, uploaded files, history, and retry credentials. Store them privately.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetPath`: `string`. Required.
- `expectedDatasetId`: `UUID`
- `savePath`: `string`. Required.
- `overwrite`: `boolean`

Returns `{ kind: "exported", savedPath }`.

#### `dohc dataset prepareRecovery`

Check a recovery archive before restoring it.

sourcePath ends in .dohc-recovery. A relative sourcePath is read only and resolves from the caller folder. Review the result before claimRecovery.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `sourcePath`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "recovery-prepared", recovery: { transferId, manifestSha256, sourceCursor, revision } | null }`.

#### `dohc dataset claimRecovery`

Restore a Collection from a prepared archive.

Set `workspaceId` to `recovery.sourceCursor.workspaceId` from `prepareRecovery`. Set `transferId` to `recovery.transferId` from `prepareRecovery`.
